subject: 英語
stem: Look at the picture. The woman is putting ___ on the cake.

options.C: plates
options.D: strawberries

explain:
解題關鍵：圖中女子正把有火焰的蠟燭插在蛋糕上；生日蛋糕上用來點亮、許願的就是 candles，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：candles，意為「蠟燭」；圖中可見她手拿蠟燭插在蛋糕上，符合。
(B)選項原文：forks，意為「叉子」；叉子放在桌上，並不是她正放上蛋糕的東西。
(C)選項原文：plates，意為「盤子」；盤子用來盛裝食物，不會插在蛋糕上。
(D)選項原文：strawberries，意為「草莓」；蛋糕上雖有水果裝飾，但她手中拿的是蠟燭，不是草莓。

subject: 英語
stem: The movie starts at two o’clock, ___ let’s meet at the theater at one forty-five.

options.C: if
options.D: because

explain:
解題關鍵：電影兩點開始，因此約在一點四十五分在戲院碰面；前後是原因與結果，應用 so（所以），故選 A。
(A)選項原文：so，表「所以」，能接出因電影兩點開演而提早十五分鐘見面的結果。
(B)選項原文：or，表「或者」，句子不是提供兩種選擇，語意不合。
(C)選項原文：if，表「如果」，前句沒有假設條件，不能使用。
(D)選項原文：because，表「因為」，通常引出原因；此處後句是安排見面的結果。

subject: 英語
stem: Peter is afraid of the dark. He even leaves the ___ on when sleeping.

options.C: lights
options.D: music

explain:
解題關鍵：Peter 害怕黑暗，睡覺時會把燈開著；能消除黑暗的複數名詞是 lights，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：computer，意為「電腦」；開著電腦不必然能照亮房間。
(B)選項原文：fans，意為「電風扇」；電風扇可送風，無法解決怕黑。
(C)選項原文：lights，意為「燈」；leave the lights on 是「讓燈開著」，符合語境。
(D)選項原文：music，意為「音樂」；音樂不能提供光線。

subject: 英語
stem: Pam is a ___ baseball player; she has more fans than any other player on her team.

options.C: popular
options.D: rich

explain:
解題關鍵：她的球迷比隊上任何一位球員都多，表示她很受歡迎；popular 正是「受歡迎的」，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：boring，意為「無聊的」；無聊的球員不會由「球迷最多」推得出來。
(B)選項原文：heavy，意為「重的」；重量與球迷數量沒有關係。
(C)選項原文：popular，意為「受歡迎的」；球迷很多正是她受歡迎的證據。
(D)選項原文：rich，意為「有錢的」；題幹沒有談到收入或財產。

subject: 英語
stem: I did not do my homework, so my teacher said I ___ stay after school to finish it.

options.C: hoped to
options.D: used to

explain:
解題關鍵：因為沒寫作業，老師要求我放學後留下完成，表過去「不得不」做某事要用 had to，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：failed to，意為「未能」，後面接原形動詞，但「未能留下」與老師的要求相反。
(B)選項原文：had to，意為「不得不」；had to stay 正確表達過去受到要求而必須留下。
(C)選項原文：hoped to，意為「希望」；留下完成作業是被要求，不是單純希望。
(D)選項原文：used to，意為「過去常常」；不表示這次因沒寫作業而必須留下。

subject: 英語
stem: Kevin has only enough money for the bag or the shoes. That is a hard ___ to make because he likes them both.

options.C: rule
options.D: trick

explain:
解題關鍵：Kevin 的錢只能買包包或鞋子之一，又兩樣都喜歡，因此難的是做「選擇」；a hard choice to make 搭配正確，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：choice，意為「選擇」；在兩樣喜歡的物品中二選一，完全符合。
(B)選項原文：gift，意為「禮物」；題幹是在決定要買什麼，不是在送禮。
(C)選項原文：rule，意為「規則」；沒有任何規則需要制定。
(D)選項原文：trick，意為「把戲、訣竅」；二選一是購物決定，不是把戲。

subject: 英語
stem: It was ___ for us to answer the math question because we’ve done the same kind of questions many times.

options.C: safe
options.D: special

explain:
解題關鍵：同類型數學題已做過很多次，所以回答起來不困難；easy 表「容易的」，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：common，意為「常見的」；題型可能常見，但空格描述的是「回答」的難易。
(B)選項原文：easy，意為「容易的」；累積多次練習使答題變容易，符合。
(C)選項原文：safe，意為「安全的」；安全與數學題是否答得出來無關。
(D)選項原文：special，意為「特別的」；多次做過反而不是強調特別。

subject: 英語
stem: Although it took me lots of time ___ a big meal for ten people, I was happy that everyone enjoyed it.

options.C: preparing
options.D: prepared

explain:
解題關鍵：it took + 人 + 時間 + to V 表示「某人花多少時間做某事」；因此應為 took me lots of time to prepare，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：prepare，原形動詞；take 花時間後不能直接接原形。
(B)選項原文：to prepare，不定詞；符合 it took me time to V 的固定句型。
(C)選項原文：preparing，動名詞；雖可說 spend time V-ing，但不能套在 took me time 後。
(D)選項原文：prepared，過去式／過去分詞；此處需要表目的或所花時間做的動作，不用過去式。

subject: 英語
stem: Don’t let the children swim in the river. We don’t know how ___ it is. It could be dangerous.

options.C: long
options.D: thick

explain:
解題關鍵：河裡游泳可能危險，是因為不知道水有多深；how deep 用來問水深，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：deep，意為「深的」；用於河水深度，且可能太深而危險。
(B)選項原文：far，意為「遠的」；不描述河水由水面到河底的深度。
(C)選項原文：long，意為「長的」；河流長度不是此處游泳的直接危險。
(D)選項原文：thick，意為「厚的」；通常描述物體厚度，不用來說河水。

subject: 英語
stem: Bob is ___ of the boys in the family. He never does any housework. His brothers at least take out the garbage sometimes.

options.C: the lazier
options.D: the laziest

explain:
解題關鍵：Bob 在家中所有男孩裡最不做家事，後句還和至少會倒垃圾的兄弟比較，故用最高級 the laziest，選 D。
(A)選項原文：lazier，是比較級「較懶」；最高級範圍是所有男孩，不能只用比較級。
(B)選項原文：the lazy，lazy 是原級形容詞，不能表示「最懶」。
(C)選項原文：the lazier，雖有 the，仍是比較級，缺少比較對象且不合最高級語意。
(D)選項原文：the laziest，最高級「最懶的」；符合 of the boys in the family。

subject: 英語
stem: Aunt Gina has lived in this town for more than sixty years, so she ___ it very well.

options.C: knows
options.D: was going to know

explain:
解題關鍵：住在這個鎮六十多年是到現在累積的經驗，結論是她現在很了解這裡；應用現在簡單式 knows，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：will know，未來式；題幹說的是她現在已熟悉，不是將來才知道。
(B)選項原文：knew，過去式；沒有表示她現在已不再了解。
(C)選項原文：knows，現在式；描述目前持續的知識與狀態，正確。
(D)選項原文：was going to know，過去未來式；需有過去觀點，題幹沒有。

subject: 英語
stem: We won’t see the sun even after the typhoon leaves, because the news said that heavier rain will soon ___.

options.C: move
options.D: stop

explain:
解題關鍵：颱風離開後仍看不到太陽，因為新聞說更大的雨很快會接著來；follow 表「接著發生」，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：catch，意為「抓住」；雨不會「抓住」前面的天氣。
(B)選項原文：follow，意為「接著發生」；heavier rain will soon follow 表示更大的雨隨後到來。
(C)選項原文：move，意為「移動」；未說雨要移往何處，且不合此搭配。
(D)選項原文：stop，意為「停止」；若雨停止就可能見到陽光，和語意相反。

subject: 英語
stem: Yesterday when I got home from work, my brother ___ for dinner, so he invited me to join him.

options.C: has gone out
options.D: was going out

explain:
解題關鍵：我昨天到家時，哥哥正要出去吃晚餐，才會邀我一起；過去某一時刻原本將要做的事用 was going out，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：goes out，現在式；時間副詞 Yesterday 要求過去時態。
(B)選項原文：went out，表示已經出去了；若已離開就無法當場邀我。
(C)選項原文：has gone out，現在完成式；不與明確過去時間 Yesterday 搭配。
(D)選項原文：was going out，表示當時正準備出去；能合理解釋邀請。

subject: 英語
stem: You were ___ not to lend Amy money. She never gives back what she borrows.

options.C: wise
options.D: wrong

explain:
解題關鍵：Amy 從不歸還借來的錢，因此你沒有借她錢是明智的判斷；wise 表「明智的」，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：crazy，意為「瘋狂的」；不借給不還錢的人並不瘋狂。
(B)選項原文：helpful，意為「有幫助的」；此處評價的是決定是否明智，不是是否幫忙。
(C)選項原文：wise，意為「明智的」；根據她不還錢的習慣，不借錢是正確判斷。
(D)選項原文：wrong，意為「錯的」；後句提供理由支持你做對了。

subject: 英語
stem: Have you found a summer job yet? Mr. Firth ___ someone to take care of his kids during the vacation. Maybe you can talk to him.

options.C: looks for
options.D: was looking for

explain:
解題關鍵：「你找到暑期工作了嗎」和「也許你可找他談」顯示 Firth 先生目前正在找人照顧孩子；現在進行式 is looking for 最合適，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：has looked for，現在完成式強調已完成或經驗，沒有凸顯目前的徵人需求。
(B)選項原文：is looking for，表示現在正在尋找；與暑假徵人及建議去談最吻合。
(C)選項原文：looks for，現在簡單式偏向習慣；題幹是眼前的職缺。
(D)選項原文：was looking for，過去進行式；沒有過去時間點，也不利於「現在去談」。

subject: 英語
stem: David looked out of the balcony window and saw a woman get in his car ___ away.

options.C: and drive
options.D: and drove

explain:
解題關鍵：saw 後可接受詞加原形動詞，表示看見動作完整發生；woman get in his car and drive away 串連兩個原形動作，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：drive，若直接接在 car 後會成為 get in his car drive away，缺少連接兩個動作的 and。
(B)選項原文：drove，過去式不能和 saw 後的原形 get 並列。
(C)選項原文：and drive，and 連接 get 與 drive 兩個原形動詞，句型正確。
(D)選項原文：and drove，and 後應和 get 同為原形，不能改成過去式。

subject: 英語
stem: The police haven’t found the little girl who ___ at a supermarket. They’ll keep doing all they can to find her.

options.C: has taken away
options.D: was taken away

explain:
解題關鍵：小女孩是在超市被人帶走，是動作承受者；who 引導的關係子句要用被動語態 was taken away，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：took away，主動過去式，會變成女孩帶走別人，角色顛倒。
(B)選項原文：taken away，只有過去分詞，前面沒有 be 動詞，句子不完整。
(C)選項原文：has taken away，現在完成主動式，仍表示女孩帶走別人。
(D)選項原文：was taken away，過去被動式，正確表達女孩被帶走。

subject: 英語
stem: Buses to the airport only come once every hour, and we just missed ___. Why don’t we take a taxi?

options.C: one
options.D: them

explain:
解題關鍵：機場巴士每小時一班，剛錯過的是「一班巴士」；one 可代替前面提到的單數可數名詞 bus，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：another，意為「另一個」；泛指另一班，不精確代回剛錯過的那一班。
(B)選項原文：it，代替特定單數事物；此處要代替同類名詞中的一班 bus，應用 one。
(C)選項原文：one，可代替單數可數名詞 bus；we just missed one 正確。
(D)選項原文：them，是複數受格；前面指一班巴士，數不一致。

subject: 英語
stem: Ariel ___ every night for a week before her Chinese test and got a very good grade.

options.C: has studied
options.D: was going to study

explain:
解題關鍵：考試前一週每晚讀書，以及後來得到好成績，都是已結束的過去事件；應用過去式 studied，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：studied，過去式；正確描述已完成的一週讀書行為。
(B)選項原文：studies，現在式；和 before her Chinese test 的過去情境不合。
(C)選項原文：has studied，現在完成式；通常不和已結束的 before test 時段搭配。
(D)選項原文：was going to study，表示原本打算讀，沒有表達實際讀了一週。

subject: 英語
stem: While reading this story, Brad saw the word “trolling” and didn’t know what it meant. Josh turned off the screen and sat back. “Why are they trolling me like this?” He didn’t understand. They wanted him to share what he thought about the show, and he did. And now look what he got. In the end, all they wanted was nice words. He found several meanings of the word in a dictionary. Which one should Brad choose?

options.B: To make someone or something move around.
options.C: To pull a fishing line through the water, often from a boat.
options.D: To write something on the Internet to hurt someone or make them angry.

explain:
解題關鍵：Josh 在網路上分享對節目的看法後，別人留言讓他受傷又生氣；此語境的 trolling 是故意用網路內容惹人不快，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：To celebrate in song.，意為「以歌慶祝」；故事沒有唱歌或慶祝的情節。
(B)選項原文：To make someone or something move around.，意為「使人或物移動」；與螢幕上的惡意留言無關。
(C)選項原文：To pull a fishing line through the water, often from a boat.，是釣魚時拖曳釣線；沒有船或釣魚情境。
(D)選項原文：To write something on the Internet to hurt someone or make them angry.，正是網路上故意傷人或惹人生氣的行為，符合。

subject: 英語
stem: What does Tea-Rock celebrate?

options.B: The coming out of their 20th kind of tea.
options.C: Their 20th year of business.
options.D: The opening of their 20th store in the USA.

explain:
解題關鍵：海報寫著 Thank You for Being with Us for Twenty Summers & Winters，表示感謝顧客陪伴二十個寒暑，也就是營業二十週年，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：Their sales in 20 countries.，意為在二十國的銷售；海報沒有提到國家或銷售量。
(B)選項原文：The coming out of their 20th kind of tea.，意為第廿種茶上市；圖中只提 Tea-Rock 20 活動，未說推出新茶。
(C)選項原文：Their 20th year of business.，意為營業二十週年；Twenty Summers & Winters 是二十年的直接證據。
(D)選項原文：The opening of their 20th store in the USA.，意為美國第廿間店開幕；獎品是去紐約的機票，不表示在美國開店。
passage: （註：address 地址）
group_title: 第21–22題題組

subject: 英語
stem: Here is the postcard Jason is going to send to Tea-Rock 20. What else does he need to put on the postcard before he sends it?

options.C: His birthday.
options.D: Another picture of the tea cup.

explain:
解題關鍵：活動要求明信片寫姓名、生日、電話、電子信箱與最愛的茶；Jason 已寫姓名、電話、信箱、最愛的茶，也貼好兩張茶杯圖，唯獨缺生日，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：His age.，意為年齡；活動規定要寫 birthday，不是年齡。
(B)選項原文：His address.，意為地址；明信片已寫寄件地址與收件地址，活動也未要求他的住址。
(C)選項原文：His birthday.，意為生日；圖上的 Jason 資料中沒有生日，正是缺漏項目。
(D)選項原文：Another picture of the tea cup.，意為再一張茶杯圖；明信片上已有兩張，符合 collect two 的要求。
passage: （註：address 地址）
group_title: 第21–22題題組

subject: 英語
stem: What can we learn about sugar from the infographic?

options.A: There are 4 g of sugar in 66 g of ice cream.
options.B: A woman can eat as much sugar a day as a man can.
options.C: Taiwan eats more sugar for each person than the US does.
options.D: 400 ml of rice milk has less sugar than 400 ml of grape juice.

explain:
解題關鍵：資訊圖以湯匙數表示糖量：400 ml rice milk 有 6 匙，400 ml grape juice 有 10 匙，因此米漿糖較少，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：There are 4 g of sugar in 66 g of ice cream.，圖示的 4 g 是「每一茶匙糖」的換算，不是說 66 g 冰淇淋只含 4 g 糖。
(B)選項原文：A woman can eat as much sugar a day as a man can.，圖示建議女性 6 匙、男性 9 匙，數量不同。
(C)選項原文：Taiwan eats more sugar for each person than the US does.，臺灣為 17.75 匙、美國為 18.75 匙，臺灣較少。
(D)選項原文：400 ml of rice milk has less sugar than 400 ml of grape juice.，米漿 6 匙少於葡萄汁 10 匙，正確。

subject: 英語
stem: What can be a reason why the list of “Sugar that is hidden in foods and drinks” is put in the infographic?

options.A: To help us understand how sugar hurts our body.
options.B: To show what kinds of foods and drinks are popular with children.
options.C: To tell us that we often have more sugar than we can without knowing it.
options.D: To let us know how much sugar is enough to make foods and drinks taste good.

explain:
解題關鍵：「Sugar that is hidden」列出冰淇淋、果汁、米漿等日常食物飲料中的糖，目的在提醒人們糖常藏在不易察覺處，可能不知不覺吃過量，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：To help us understand how sugar hurts our body.，糖如何傷身由左下方的身體影響圖說明，不是這份隱藏糖清單的主要功能。
(B)選項原文：To show what kinds of foods and drinks are popular with children.，清單沒有比較兒童喜好。
(C)選項原文：To tell us that we often have more sugar than we can without knowing it.，用常見品項與匙數呈現隱藏糖，正是在提醒不自覺攝取過多。
(D)選項原文：To let us know how much sugar is enough to make foods and drinks taste good.，圖中沒有討論食物要加多少糖才好吃。
passage:

stem: Which idea is talked about in the first paragraph of the reading?

options.A: How you should do Tabata training.
options.B: What is the best time for Tabata training. （註：paragraph 段落 ）

explain:
解題關鍵：第一段說明每次運動 20 秒、休息 10 秒、至少重複八次，並列舉動作與可自行選擇的部位，重點是進行方法，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：How you should do Tabata training.，段落提供秒數、休息與動作安排，正是做法。
(B)選項原文：What is the best time for Tabata training. （註：paragraph 段落 ），文中沒有說一天中何時做最好。
(C)選項原文：Who first had the idea of Tabata training.，沒有介紹發明者或創始者。
(D)選項原文：How often you should do Tabata training.，at least eight times 指一回訓練的重複次數，非一週或一天的頻率。
passage:
Tabata training is a very popular way of exercising these days. It doesn’t take much time or space, and it burns calories faster than other ways of exercising. The idea of Tabata training is simple: exercise for 20 seconds, rest for 10 seconds, and then repeat (at least eight times). The moves for the 20-second exercise are not difficult to learn. Jumping jacks, high knees, squats, and planks are some of the most common moves. You can decide yourself what moves to do in your Tabata training. For example, you can do more leg exercises if you want strong legs.

One great thing about Tabata training is that your body will keep burning calories for at least an hour after 4 minutes of Tabata training. But to have this wonderful “afterburn,” you need to exercise really hard during each 20 seconds. If you seldom exercise or have heart problems, this exercise may not be good for you. But for people who enjoy exercising but are too busy to go to the gym, Tabata training might just be the answer. （註：calorie 卡路里(熱量單位)）

explain:
解題關鍵：報告先說長工時造成死亡問題，交代為何有 No Overtime Day（c）；再定義這一天的規定（a）；接著說員工如何仍繼續工作（d）；最後分析制度失敗的升遷加薪誘因（b），故選 D。
(A)選項原文：acdb.，把制度內容放在問題成因之前，與文章先談長工時危害的順序不符。

(C)選項原文：cabd.，把失敗原因的薪資升遷分析放在員工實際繞過規定之前，與文章不符。
(D)選項原文：cadb.，依文章從問題、制度、員工反應到失敗原因的順序，正確。
passage:
The problem of long working hours is a real headache in our country. It kills many people every year (see Figure 1), and many companies are trying to change that. They have at least one “No Overtime Day” in a week, and it is often Wednesday. On “No Overtime Day,” workers are asked to leave their offices before 8 p.m. At 8 p.m., companies play the song “There’s Always Tomorrow” and turn off all the lights. However, after the workers walk out of their offices, they don’t go home. Some go back later, turn on their table lamps, and keep working, and others find somewhere else to work until very late at night. Restaurants and coffee shops are busier on Wednesday evenings, and they have started selling drinks and meals for these workers. But why do these people keep working? A study shows that workers who work more hours often have a bigger chance to get paid more and rise higher in their companies. This is true for both men and women (see Figure 2). Working long hours has become a way to show that people are hard-working. Clearly, this must be changed before the problem gets any worse.

Language and Power: Cameroon’s Story By Elisa Grant, 2 Oct 2017

In the modern world, being able to speak English is often a way to get power. However, this is not true for English speakers in Cameroon. To know why things are different in this African country, we need to go back one hundred years.

In 1919, Kamerun (the name of Cameroon at the time) was cut into two parts: one belonged to France, and the other belonged to the UK. In 1960, the French Cameroon became the Republic of Cameroun, and the UK’s part joined it in 1961. The new country changed its name to the Federal Republic of Cameroon. Although both French and English are Cameroon’s official languages, only around 20% of its people speak English. Also, the government has been in French speakers’ hands since the two parts became one country.

For a long time, Cameroon’s English speakers have felt they are not welcome in their own country. For example, it is very difficult for them to find jobs in the government, and they are often asked to speak French in business and at official events. They have become more resentful at the government and decided to fight for themselves. Since last year, the English speakers have tried to build their own country. Yesterday, they said in a public meeting that they were not part of Cameroon anymore. They are now a new country, “Ambazonia.” When the police tried to stop the meeting, at least eight people were killed. Read more

In the modern world, being able to speak English is often a way to get power. However, this is not true for English speakers in Cameroon. To know why things are different in this African country, we need to go back one hundred years.

In 1919, Kamerun (the name of Cameroon at the time) was cut into two parts: one belonged to France, and the other belonged to the UK. In 1960, the French Cameroon became the Republic of Cameroun, and the UK’s part joined it in 1961. The new country changed its name to the Federal Republic of Cameroon. Although both French and English are Cameroon’s official languages, only around 20% of its people speak English. Also, the government has been in French speakers’ hands since the two parts became one country.

For a long time, Cameroon’s English speakers have felt they are not welcome in their own country. For example, it is very difficult for them to find jobs in the government, and they are often asked to speak French in business and at official events. They have become more resentful at the government and decided to fight for themselves. Since last year, the English speakers have tried to build their own country. Yesterday, they said in a public meeting that they were not part of Cameroon anymore. They are now a new country, “Ambazonia.” When the police tried to stop the meeting, at least eight people were killed. Read more

THE SOUTHEND TRAIL has been popular with nature lovers for years. The 120-km trail passes beautiful lakes, crosses rivers, and goes through mountains and hills. This gives bird lovers some of the best places for birdwatching. The trail also takes you to the Southend Museum and to two famous castles, Edward Castle and Sloan Castle. It’s best to plan one day for one part of the trail and start your hike early in the morning, because each part takes at least seven hours. If you don’t want to walk, you can bike, but make sure you stay on the main trail, because the side trails are not wide enough for biking. There are two types of lodging for visitors. options.C: of course
options.D: for example

explain:
解題關鍵：空格後列出 eye、Bob、my gym 等 palindrome 的實例，因此需要引出例子的片語 for example，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：in fact，意為「事實上」；用來補充或修正說法，不是列舉例子。
(B)選項原文：at first，意為「起初」；文章沒有前後時間順序。
(C)選項原文：of course，意為「當然」；不能自然引出一串定義的例子。
(D)選項原文：for example，意為「例如」；後接多個 palindrome 範例，搭配正確。
passage:
English words are made of 26 letters, and palindromes and anagrams are two kinds of word games about spelling. A palindrome is a word or a sentence that reads the same from left to right or from right to left, 40 , “eye,” “Bob,” “my gym,” and “Was it a car or a cat I saw?” An anagram of a word or words is made by putting the letters of the word or words in a different way. Look at the words and their anagrams below. Can you think of other possible anagrams of these words?

Anagrams are often longer words that don’t really mean anything but are fun to say. Sometimes they can even mean something 42 , like when a common word, “restaurant,” becomes “Eat rats, run!” Actually, palindromes and anagrams are 43 . Palindromes can be used to learn mathematics and make music. Anagrams are also a good way to hide something. In history, people often hid their important studies in anagrams. Can you think of any other way to use them?

options.C: it makes

(C)選項原文：it makes，所用字母與 mistake 完全一致，只是排列不同，正確。
(D)選項原文：me steak，含有第二個 e，且缺少 i，字母數量不一致。

subject: 英語
stem: Look at the picture. The man is holding a ___ of grapes in his hands.

options.C: bowl
options.D: box

explain:
解題關鍵：圖中男子雙手抱著一個裝滿葡萄、可提拿的編織容器，應是 basket（籃子），故選 B。
(A)選項原文：bag 是「袋子」，不是圖中的籃子。
(B)選項原文：basket 是「籃子」，符合圖片中的容器與一串串葡萄。
(C)選項原文：bowl 是「碗」，通常較小且不用雙手抱著裝葡萄。
(D)選項原文：box 是「盒子」，多為有硬邊的盒狀容器，與圖不符。

subject: 英語
stem: Dennis enjoys ___ in public. He is proud of his beautiful voice.

options.C: shopping
options.D: singing

explain:
解題關鍵：Dennis 為自己的 beautiful voice 感到驕傲，表示他喜歡在公共場合唱歌；enjoy 後面要接 V-ing，故選 D singing。
(A)選項原文：dancing 是「跳舞」，與 beautiful voice 的線索無關。
(B)選項原文：drawing 是「畫畫」，不會以聲音優美為理由。
(C)選項原文：shopping 是「購物」，也和聲音沒有關係。
(D)選項原文：singing 是「唱歌」，既符合語意，也符合 enjoy + V-ing。

subject: 英語
stem: Mrs. Johnson can’t hear very well. If you need to talk to her, you must ___.

options.C: listen
options.D: shout

explain:
解題關鍵：Mrs. Johnson 聽力不好，和她說話時必須提高音量喊叫，故選 D shout。
(A)選項原文：explain 是「解釋」，不表示提高音量。
(B)選項原文：hurry 是「趕快」，不能解決她聽不清楚的問題。
(C)選項原文：listen 是「聽」，是她要做的事，空格卻是在說話者必須做的事。
(D)選項原文：shout 是「大聲喊」，最能讓聽力不好的人聽見。

subject: 英語
stem: People got very excited when they watched Ms. Smith ___ at the party.

options.C: has danced
options.D: to dance

explain:
解題關鍵：watch 後可接受詞加 V-ing，表示看見某人正在做某事；大家在派對上看著 Ms. Smith 跳舞，故選 B dancing。
(A)選項原文：danced 是過去式，不能直接接在 watched Ms. Smith 後表達此結構。
(B)選項原文：dancing 是現在分詞，watch + 人 + V-ing 表示觀看動作進行中。
(C)選項原文：has danced 是現在完成式，不能放在此受詞補語位置。
(D)選項原文：to dance 雖有 watch + 人 + 原形動詞的用法，但不是 to V。

subject: 英語
stem: I tried on these shoes in several different ___, and I thought the white pair looked best on me.

options.C: shapes
options.D: sizes

explain:
解題關鍵：後句說白色那一雙看起來最好，白色是顏色，故選 A colors。
(A)選項原文：colors 是「顏色」，可搭配 white pair，符合語意。
(B)選項原文：prices 是「價格」，白色不是價格。
(C)選項原文：shapes 是「形狀」，題幹沒有比較鞋子的形狀。
(D)選項原文：sizes 是「尺寸」，white 不能用來說明尺寸。

subject: 英語
stem: Rex did not feel the earthquake this morning. He ___ in the park at the time.

options.C: has jogged
options.D: would jog

explain:
解題關鍵：at the time 指地震發生的那個過去時刻，Rex 當時正在公園慢跑，所以用過去進行式 was jogging，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：jogged 是單純過去式，沒有凸顯地震發生當下動作正在進行。
(B)選項原文：was jogging 是過去進行式，正確表達「當時正在慢跑」。
(C)選項原文：has jogged 是現在完成式，不能和明確過去時間 this morning at the time 搭配。
(D)選項原文：would jog 常表過去習慣或假設，非此刻正在發生的動作。

subject: 英語
stem: Mr. Lee has worked in the same store for ten years; he’s never thought about ___ his job.

options.C: remembering
options.D: starting

explain:
解題關鍵：think about 後面要接名詞或 V-ing；「想過換工作」是 think about changing his job，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：changing 是動名詞，和 think about 搭配正確，意為「更換」。
(B)選項原文：finding 是「找到」，find his job 不是此處「換工作」的意思。
(C)選項原文：remembering 是「記得」，語意不合。
(D)選項原文：starting 是「開始」，starting his job 也不符合已做十年工作的情境。

subject: 英語
stem: I didn’t take the bus today because it was ___. All the seats were taken and a lot of students were standing.

options.C: full
options.D: wrong

explain:
解題關鍵：所有座位都有人坐，還有許多學生站著，說明公車已經滿了，故選 C full。
(A)選項原文：dirty 是「髒的」，與座位全被坐滿無關。
(B)選項原文：fast 是「快速的」，不能解釋乘客站立。
(C)選項原文：full 是「滿的」，正好呼應 all the seats were taken。
(D)選項原文：wrong 是「錯誤的」，不適合形容公車擁擠狀態。

subject: 英語
stem: Don’t go away when you’re cooking, ___ the food might burn.

options.C: or
options.D: so

explain:
解題關鍵：句型「祈使句 + or + 結果」表示「否則」；不要走開，否則食物可能燒焦，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：but 是「但是」，不能連出警告的後果。
(B)選項原文：if 是「如果」，後面應形成條件子句，結構不合。
(C)選項原文：or 是「否則」，可接 food might burn 表示不照做的結果。
(D)選項原文：so 是「所以」，會變成「不要走開，所以食物可能燒焦」，邏輯相反。

subject: 英語
stem: Jerry wanted to know ___ he was kicked off the soccer team, but no one gave him a good reason.

options.C: whether
options.D: why

explain:
解題關鍵：Jerry 想知道自己為何被踢出足球隊，而後句說沒人給他好的 reason，空格應填詢問原因的 why，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：where 詢問地點，與 reason 不相符。
(B)選項原文：when 詢問時間，不是被踢出隊的原因。
(C)選項原文：whether 表示「是否」，不能對應 a good reason。
(D)選項原文：why 詢問「為什麼」，正好對應後面的 reason。

subject: 英語
stem: Jenny is already forty, doesn’t have a job and often makes trouble for her parents. To them, she is really a(n) ___.

options.C: gift
options.D: headache

explain:
解題關鍵：Jenny 四十歲沒工作，還常替父母惹麻煩；headache 可比喻令人煩惱的人或事，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：daughter 是「女兒」，只是身分，無法表達父母的困擾。
(B)選項原文：example 是「例子、榜樣」，與惹麻煩的語氣相反。
(C)選項原文：gift 是「禮物」，帶正面意思，不合情境。
(D)選項原文：headache 本義是「頭痛」，此處比喻「麻煩人物」，最貼切。

subject: 英語
stem: Ed and Jill ___ camping this weekend, so they have to finish their homework by Friday.

options.C: are going
options.D: have gone

explain:
解題關鍵：this weekend 是已安排好的未來計畫，現在進行式可表示近期確定安排；Ed 和 Jill 要去露營，故選 C are going。
(A)選項原文：went 是過去式，和 this weekend 的未來時間不合。
(B)選項原文：were going 是過去進行式，沒有過去時間脈絡。
(C)選項原文：are going 可表示已安排的未來行程，符合語意。
(D)選項原文：have gone 表示已經去且尚未回來，和還得在週五前寫作業矛盾。

subject: 英語
stem: Doraemon, a blue Japanese robot cat, has hated mice since his ears ___ by a mouse.

options.C: were bitten
options.D: have bitten

explain:
解題關鍵：耳朵是被老鼠咬的受事，且事件發生在過去，所以用過去式被動語態 were bitten，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：bit 是主動過去式，會變成耳朵咬老鼠，語意顛倒。
(B)選項原文：bite 是原形動詞，時態與被動語意都不合。
(C)選項原文：were bitten 是「被咬了」，主詞 ears 為複數，形式正確。
(D)選項原文：have bitten 是現在完成主動，仍是耳朵去咬別人，且時態不合。

subject: 英語
stem: If we play some interesting games in class, there ___ more fun in learning English.

options.C: will be
options.D: will have

explain:
解題關鍵：第一類條件句中，If 子句用現在式 play，主要子句用 will + 原形動詞；there be 的未來式是 there will be，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：are 是現在式，未表達遊戲帶來的未來結果。
(B)選項原文：has 不可接在 there 後，且 fun 是不可數名詞，不用 has。
(C)選項原文：will be 符合 If + 現在式，will + 原形動詞的條件句規則。
(D)選項原文：will have 不可用在 there 的存在句型；應是 there will be fun。

subject: 英語
stem: The ___ of this shop was so bad; I never got any answer after I emailed them my questions.

options.C: price
options.D: service

explain:
解題關鍵：寄信詢問卻從未收到回答，問題在商店提供給顧客的服務很差，故選 D service。
(A)選項原文：item 是「商品」，商品本身不會回覆電子郵件。
(B)選項原文：business 是「生意、公司」，不精確指稱回覆顧客的品質。
(C)選項原文：price 是「價格」，與沒有回信無關。
(D)選項原文：service 是「服務」，customer service 差正可解釋沒有答覆。

subject: 英語
stem: It’s not easy to see those islands clearly from here on sunny days, and it’s even less ___ to see them on cloudy days.

options.C: possible
options.D: special

explain:
解題關鍵：晴天已不容易看清島嶼，陰天能看清的可能性更低；less 後接形容詞 possible，形成 less possible，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：difficult 是「困難的」，less difficult 反而表示較不困難，與 even less 的意思相反。
(B)選項原文：lucky 是「幸運的」，不能形容看見島嶼是否可行。
(C)選項原文：possible 是「可能的」，less possible 表示更不可能，符合上下文。
(D)選項原文：special 是「特別的」，與天候造成能否看見無關。

subject: 英語
stem: Do you remember the CD I was looking for for months? I ___ found it in a small shop. Look, here it is!

options.C: finally
options.D: still

explain:
解題關鍵：找了好幾個月後，現在終於在小店找到 CD，應用 finally 表「終於」，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：almost 是「幾乎」，幾乎找到不等於已拿出 CD 給人看。
(B)選項原文：even 是「甚至」，不能表達長時間尋找後的結果。
(C)選項原文：finally 是「終於」，呼應 for months 與 Look, here it is。
(D)選項原文：still 是「仍然」，若仍在找就不會說已找到。

subject: 英語
stem: Business at Jane’s shop has not been good these days. And the new supermarket across the street only makes things ___.

options.C: more boring
options.D: more convenient

explain:
解題關鍵：Jane 的店生意已不好，對街新超市增加競爭，只會讓情況更糟；make things worse 是固定用法，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：easier 是「更容易」，與競爭使生意惡化相反。
(B)選項原文：worse 是「更糟」，最符合生意不佳又遇到新超市的情境。
(C)選項原文：more boring 是「更無聊」，不能形容營業狀況變差。
(D)選項原文：more convenient 是「更方便」，也不是 Jane 生意受影響的重點。

subject: 英語
stem: Scott wasn’t sure if the young woman before him was ___ pulled him out of a car on fire.

options.C: the one she
options.D: the one who

explain:
解題關鍵：Scott 不確定眼前女子是否就是把他從失火車中拉出來的那個人；the one 後要用關係代名詞 who 指人並引導子句，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：who 只能直接指人，放在 was 後缺少「那個人」的名詞核心。
(B)選項原文：the one 有「那個人」，但後面直接接 pulled，缺少連接關係子句的 who。
(C)選項原文：the one she 後面會變成 she pulled him，主詞與句意不對。
(D)選項原文：the one who 完整表示「拉他出來的那個人」，結構與語意都正確。

subject: 英語
stem: I ___ swimming for several years before I went to this high school. I gave it up because of heavy schoolwork.

options.C: practiced
options.D: would practice

explain:
解題關鍵：游泳練了數年這件事發生在進入這所高中之前，後來又因課業放棄，都是已結束的過去經驗，用過去式 practiced，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：have practiced 是現在完成式，通常與現在有連結，卻和 before I went to this high school 的過去時間不合。
(B)選項原文：am practicing 是現在進行式，和 I gave it up 矛盾。
(C)選項原文：practiced 是過去式，正確說明進高中前曾練習游泳。
(D)選項原文：would practice 可表過去習慣，但此處要說明一段已結束的經驗，過去式最恰當。

subject: 英語
stem: Frank Kane is so good in the movie that many people ___ he will win the best actor prize.

options.C: notice
options.D: plan

explain:
解題關鍵：Frank Kane 演得非常好，因此許多人預期他會得最佳男主角獎；expect 後可接子句，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：expect 是「預期」，符合根據演技推測得獎。
(B)選項原文：forget 是「忘記」，不能合理接他會得獎的判斷。
(C)選項原文：notice 是「注意到」，只表察覺，不表示預測。
(D)選項原文：plan 是「計畫」，人們不能替他規劃一定贏得獎項。

subject: 英語
stem: The new medicine that just came out on the market ___ thousands of lives.

options.C: saving
options.D: to save

explain:
解題關鍵：新藥剛上市後到現在已救了許多生命，強調過去發生且結果延續至今，用現在完成式 has saved，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：and saved 前面沒有可連接的並列動詞，句子缺主要動詞。
(B)選項原文：has saved 是現在完成式，主詞 medicine 為單數，形式與語意都正確。
(C)選項原文：saving 是分詞，不能單獨當本句主要動詞。
(D)選項原文：to save 是不定詞，也不能單獨作句子的謂語。

subject: 英語
stem: Now I often think of those days with Pip, my pet dog. When I read in my room, he ___ quietly beside me.

options.C: has come and sat
options.D: used to come and sit

explain:
解題關鍵：Now I often think of those days 表示回想過去；Pip 以前常常在我讀書時過來坐在旁邊，used to + 原形動詞表示過去習慣，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：will come and sit 是未來式，不能描述已逝的往日習慣。
(B)選項原文：comes and sits 是現在式，與 those days 的回憶時間不合。
(C)選項原文：has come and sat 是現在完成式，不能表達反覆的過去習慣。
(D)選項原文：used to come and sit 表示「以前常會走來坐下」，最符合情境。

subject: 英語
stem: Amy went to Four Seasons’ Kitchen with her mother after she collected 15 stars. They ordered two Garden Sandwiches, an Autumn Wind, and a Winter Snow. After using the stars, how much did they pay for their meals?
explain:
解題關鍵：圖中 Garden Sandwich 每份 $80，兩份是 $160；Autumn Wind $60、Winter Snow $70，原價共 $290。集滿 15 顆星可免費換一杯 $60 飲料，因此 Autumn Wind 免費，應付 $160 + $70 = $230，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：$290. 是未使用 15 顆星兌換飲料前的原價。
(B)選項原文：$230. 是兩份 Garden Sandwich 加上 Winter Snow 的金額，正確。
(C)選項原文：$220. 未依菜單價格與 $60 免費飲料計算。
(D)選項原文：$160. 只算到兩份三明治，漏掉 Winter Snow。
group_title: 第24–25題題組

subject: 英語
stem: Amy wants to bring her friends to Four Seasons’ Kitchen in August. She looks at her calendar to pick a time to go there. Which are the time and date she （註：calendar 月曆 can choose? ）

options.C: 3:00 pm, August 13.
options.D: 2:00 pm, August 28.

explain:
解題關鍵：店家週二至週日 2:00–8:00 pm 營業，週一及每月第二個星期日休息。8 月 11 日是週五，5:00 pm 在營業時間內；故選 B。
(A)選項原文：8:30 pm, August 1. 的 8:30 已超過晚上 8:00 打烊時間。
(B)選項原文：5:00 pm, August 11. 是週五且在 2:00–8:00 pm 之間，可以前往。
(C)選項原文：3:00 pm, August 13. 雖在營業時段，8 月 13 日是第二個星期日，店家休息。
(D)選項原文：2:00 pm, August 28. 是週一，店家固定休息。
group_title: 第24–25題題組

subject: 英語
stem: According to the notes, which is the WRONG way to help a baby bird that is out of its nest?

options.A: Feed it before you take it to a hospital.
options.B: Leave it alone if it is not hurt and has feathers.
options.C: Call the animal center if you can’t find its nest.
options.D: Put it back in its nest if it is not hurt and has few feathers.

explain:
解題關鍵：題目問 WRONG way。圖中明寫受傷小鳥可送動物醫院，但要「Keep it warm and don’t give it any food!」；因此先餵食是錯誤做法，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：Feed it before you take it to a hospital. 與圖中的 don’t give it any food! 直接衝突，是錯誤做法。
(B)選項原文：Leave it alone if it is not hurt and has feathers. 圖中說有羽毛且未受傷時 just leave it there，正確。
(C)選項原文：Call the animal center if you can’t find its nest. 圖中說羽毛少卻找不到或碰不到巢時要打給動物中心，正確。
(D)選項原文：Put it back in its nest if it is not hurt and has few feathers. 圖中說羽毛少、可碰到巢時放回去，正確。
passage: （註：nest 鳥巢 feather 羽毛）
group_title: 第26–27題題組

subject: 英語
stem: According to the notes, what do birds do if their babies have the smell of people on them?

options.A: They keep taking care of them.
options.B: They push them out of the nest.
options.C: They clean them until the smell goes away.
options.D: They leave them behind and move to a new nest.

explain:
解題關鍵：圖中先寫有人相信小鳥沾上人的味道，親鳥會放棄牠；箭頭後特別標示 WRONG! Birds don’t care!，表示親鳥仍會照顧幼鳥，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：They keep taking care of them. 符合 Birds don’t care!，人味不會使親鳥放棄幼鳥。
(B)選項原文：They push them out of the nest. 圖中沒有這項說明，且不等於 don’t care。
(C)選項原文：They clean them until the smell goes away. 圖中未提親鳥會清洗幼鳥。
(D)選項原文：They leave them behind and move to a new nest. 這正是圖中標為錯誤的迷思。
passage: （註：nest 鳥巢 feather 羽毛）

subject: 英語
stem: According to the reading, which is one of the reasons for food waste?

options.A: Stores do not know how to pack food well.
options.B: Farmers do not have enough machines to collect food.
options.C: There is no refrigerator on the truck to keep food fresh.
options.D: Factories do not have enough trucks to carry food to stores.

explain:
解題關鍵：圖表 Stage 2（On the road）列出「Do not have refrigerators to keep food fresh」，這正是運送途中食物浪費的原因，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：Stores do not know how to pack food well. 打包機器不足是 Stage 3 工廠的問題，不是商店。
(B)選項原文：Farmers do not have enough machines to collect food. 圖中農場階段沒有這項原因。
(C)選項原文：There is no refrigerator on the truck to keep food fresh. 正是 Stage 2 圖表所列原因。
(D)選項原文：Factories do not have enough trucks to carry food to stores. 圖中工廠說的是機器不足，未提卡車不足。

subject: 英語
stem: Which is true about food waste at each stage in the three parts of the world?

options.A: For each area, the highest percentage of food waste happens at Stage 5.
options.B: Europe has a lower percentage of food waste at Stage 3 than the other two areas.
options.C: North America & Oceania has a higher percentage of food waste at Stage 1 than Europe.
options.D: South & Southeast Asia has a higher percentage of food waste at Stage 4 than the other two areas.

explain:
解題關鍵：圖表 Stage 4 的數值為北美及大洋洲 2.4%、歐洲 2.2%、南亞及東南亞 4.6%，所以南亞及東南亞最高，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：For each area, the highest percentage of food waste happens at Stage 5. 南亞及東南亞最高的是 Stage 3 的 9.6%，不是 Stage 5。
(B)選項原文：Europe has a lower percentage of food waste at Stage 3 than the other two areas. 歐洲 Stage 3 是 3.9%，高於北美及大洋洲的 3.4%。
(C)選項原文：North America & Oceania has a higher percentage of food waste at Stage 1 than Europe. 北美及大洋洲是 10.5%，低於歐洲的 11.3%。
(D)選項原文：South & Southeast Asia has a higher percentage of food waste at Stage 4 than the other two areas. 其 4.6% 高於另外兩區，正確。
passage: （註：stage 階段 waste 浪費 percentage 百分比）

subject: 英語
stem: What is the trick that the mosquito uses in rain?

options.A: It shakes its body fast enough to get water off.
options.B: It drops with the raindrop and then rolls off it.
options.C: It flies behind the raindrop and pushes it away.
options.D: It rides on the raindrop and lands on the ground.

explain:
解題關鍵：文章第三段說蚊子被雨滴擊中後會和雨滴一起落下，落約 6 公分後再 roll off the raindrop 飛走，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：It shakes its body fast enough to get water off. 文中沒有說蚊子靠快速甩身體脫水。
(B)選項原文：It drops with the raindrop and then rolls off it. 正確轉述文章的保命技巧。
(C)選項原文：It flies behind the raindrop and pushes it away. 文中是被雨滴推著掉落，不是推開雨滴。
(D)選項原文：It rides on the raindrop and lands on the ground. 文中說牠會在落地前滾離雨滴並飛走。
passage:
Sometimes when the rain falls hard and fast on you, it might hurt a little. But what happens when it hits a mosquito? A 2012 study says when a raindrop falls on a mosquito, it’s like when a bus hits a person. Besides, the little insect is hit by a raindrop about once every 20 seconds. So why don’t we see many dead mosquitoes after it rains?

A mosquito is as big as a raindrop, but it is much lighter — 0.002 g only. This saves its life in raindrop attacks. Because the mosquito is so light, when it is hit by a raindrop, it won’t experience a force that is strong enough to kill it.

The study also found that when a mosquito is hit by a raindrop, the insect is pushed by the raindrop and falls together with it. But the mosquito doesn’t get wet easily because it is covered with hairs which keep off water. After dropping about 6 cm, it will roll off the raindrop and fly away.

However, this trick isn’t always successful. If the mosquito flies too low when it is hit by the raindrop, it won’t have time to fly off. Then it will hit the ground and meet its death.

（註：force 力量）
group_title: 第30–32題題組

subject: 英語
stem: What keeps a mosquito safe in the rain?

options.C: It is as big as a raindrop.
options.D: It is strong enough to fight the force of a raindrop.

explain:
解題關鍵：第二段直接說蚊子只有 0.002 g，「This saves its life」；因為很輕，受到雨滴撞擊的力不足以殺死牠，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：It is very light. 直接符合文章所說救牠一命的原因。
(B)選項原文：It has no body hairs. 文中相反，蚊子有 hairs，可幫助防水。
(C)選項原文：It is as big as a raindrop. 文章雖提大小相當，但說救命的是重量很輕。
(D)選項原文：It is strong enough to fight the force of a raindrop. 牠不是靠強壯對抗，而是因很輕承受的力不夠強。

subject: 英語
stem: When would it be dangerous for a mosquito in the rain?

options.A: When it flies too close to the ground.
options.B: When the rain falls too hard and too fast.
options.C: When it is hit by raindrops too many times.
options.D: When it drops for more than 6 cm in the rain.

explain:
解題關鍵：最後一段說若蚊子被雨滴擊中時飛得 too low，就沒有時間飛離雨滴，會撞到地面死亡，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：When it flies too close to the ground. 正確對應 flies too low 與 hit the ground。
(B)選項原文：When the rain falls too hard and too fast. 這是文章開頭引入的情境，未說必然造成危險。
(C)選項原文：When it is hit by raindrops too many times. 文章說約每 20 秒被擊中一次，未說次數多就是危險原因。
(D)選項原文：When it drops for more than 6 cm in the rain. 文中是約落 6 公分後能滾離雨滴，不是超過 6 公分才危險。

subject: 英語
stem: What do the three stories in the reading all talk about?

options.C: How “For Elise” became popular.
options.D: Why Beethoven wrote “For Elise.”

explain:
解題關鍵：三個故事分別說 Beethoven 為 Röckel 道別、為 Malfatti 寫曲卻被抄錯題名、或為教 Barensfeld 而寫；共同都在猜他為何寫這首曲子，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：Who Beethoven’s true love was. 只有 Malfatti 的故事提到他愛她，不能涵蓋三則故事。
(B)選項原文：Who played “For Elise” the best. 三則故事完全沒有比較演奏者。
(C)選項原文：How “For Elise” became popular. 文中只說手稿 1867 年被發現，並非三則故事的共同主題。
(D)選項原文：Why Beethoven wrote “For Elise.” 三則故事都提供不同寫作動機，正確。
passage:
You probably have heard Beethoven’s famous piano piece “For Elise,” but do you know who “Elise” was?

One story is that Elise was Elisabeth Röckel. She once sang in Beethoven’s opera Fidelio, and the two became very good friends. Beethoven called her “Elise.” When Röckel was leaving the city of Vienna, Beethoven wrote “For Elise” to say goodbye to her. Another story is that Elise was Therese Malfatti. Beethoven was in love with her. He wrote a piece for her and put “For Therese” on the manuscript. Malfatti kept the manuscript and left it to her family when she died. Later, a man copied the manuscript and wrote “For Elise” by mistake. There is another possible Elise: Elise Barensfeld. She learned the piano from Malfatti, the same Malfatti in the second story. To help Malfatti, Beethoven wrote the piece for her to use to teach Barensfeld.

These are just some guesses about who Elise was. We may never know the right answer. No one knew about the piece until 1867, when the manuscript was found. This was 40 years after Beethoven’s death, so he wasn’t around to tell us who Elise was. Only one thing is for sure: “For Elise” will always be enjoyed.

（註：opera 歌劇；manuscript 手稿）

stem: What do we know about “For Elise” from the reading?

options.A: It first appeared in the opera Fidelio.
options.C: The manuscript was found after Beethoven died.
options.D: The manuscript is now kept by the city of Vienna.

explain:
解題關鍵：文章明說手稿到 1867 年才被找到，且那是 Beethoven 去世 40 年後，因此手稿是在他死後才被發現，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：It first appeared in the opera Fidelio. Fidelio 是 Röckel 曾演唱的歌劇，文中未說此曲首演於其中。
(B)選項原文：The true “Elise” was Elise Barensfeld. 文章說這些都只是 guesses，真正身分未知。
(C)選項原文：The manuscript was found after Beethoven died. 與 1867 年、去世 40 年後的內容相符。

passage:
You probably have heard Beethoven’s famous piano piece “For Elise,” but do you know who “Elise” was?

One story is that Elise was Elisabeth Röckel. She once sang in Beethoven’s opera Fidelio, and the two became very good friends. Beethoven called her “Elise.” When Röckel was leaving the city of Vienna, Beethoven wrote “For Elise” to say goodbye to her. Another story is that Elise was Therese Malfatti. Beethoven was in love with her. He wrote a piece for her and put “For Therese” on the manuscript. Malfatti kept the manuscript and left it to her family when she died. Later, a man copied the manuscript and wrote “For Elise” by mistake. There is another possible Elise: Elise Barensfeld. She learned the piano from Malfatti, the same Malfatti in the second story. To help Malfatti, Beethoven wrote the piece for her to use to teach Barensfeld.

These are just some guesses about who Elise was. We may never know the right answer. No one knew about the piece until 1867, when the manuscript was found. This was 40 years after Beethoven’s death, so he wasn’t around to tell us who Elise was. Only one thing is for sure: “For Elise” will always be enjoyed.

stem: What idea does Jesse Cohen talk about in the reading?

options.A: Not all kinds of toys are helpful for children’s learning.
options.B: Parents should give their children the right toys for their age.
options.C: Children should learn about their gender from playing with toys.
options.D: We should not let gender decide which toys children can play with.

explain:
解題關鍵：文章指出孩子因觀察同性別的人而把玩具分成「男生／女生的」，這會限縮探索興趣與能力的機會；主張是不該由性別決定能玩什麼，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：Not all kinds of toys are helpful for children’s learning. 文中說不同玩具各有助益，不是說有些無助學習。
(B)選項原文：Parents should give their children the right toys for their age. 文章談性別刻板印象，不是年齡分級。
(C)選項原文：Children should learn about their gender from playing with toys. 文中把這種 watch and follow 習慣視為可能有害。
(D)選項原文：We should not let gender decide which toys children can play with. 最能概括全文觀點。
passage:
Which would you give a boy for his birthday, a toy truck or a doll? If you choose the truck, well, you’re not alone. Most people think that some toys are for boys and some are for girls. We might pick building toys for boys and kitchen toys for girls. But why do we do this? Are boys and girls really born with different interests in toys?

No, they are not. Children start to show different interests in toys at age three, but only because at this time, they begin to learn about gender and to follow what others of their gender do. If you give a girl kitchen toys, she will think they are girls’ toys because she sees other girls playing with them. But if you give a girl a toy car and show her a group of girls who are playing with cars, she’ll play with the toy car and think it is a girls’ toy. This “watch and follow” habit often becomes a rule for both boys and girls in choosing the “right” toys.

However, this rule can be bad for children. Different toys teach children different things. Dolls help with their early language use, and building toys are good for learning math and science. By playing with different toys, children can find out what they are interested in or what they are good at. If they only play one kind of toy, they may lose this important chance. They may also get a wrong idea about what boys or girls are able to do. Some doctors worry that children may use the same kind of thinking when they look for jobs in the future. If they do, they may miss something more important than just getting a chance to play with different toys. They may miss many, perhaps better, chances in life.

解題關鍵：文章從 Colvin 決定當記者、加入 Sunday Times、在多地報導戰爭，到最後因報導工作喪生，按時間介紹她的記者生涯，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：Marie Colvin’s war reports. 文章有提報導內容，但重點涵蓋她整個職業生涯與選擇。
(B)選項原文：Marie Colvin’s working life. 最完整概括她從入行、工作經歷到付出生命的歷程。

passage: Marie Colvin was a world-famous war reporter. She was born in New York, USA, in 1956 and died in Homs, Syria, in 2012. When she was a student at Yale University, Colvin decided that she wanted to be a reporter in the future. She joined the Sunday Times, a UK newspaper, in 1985 and soon became its Middle East reporter. Besides the Middle East, she also reported from other parts of the world: Chechnya, Kosovo and Sri Lanka, for example. When she was reporting on the war in Sri Lanka, she lost her left eye. But that never stopped her. She still went to dangerous places that few reporters wanted to visit and stayed when others left. Colvin showed great empathy in her stories. For her, war reporting was not just some quick interviews and a few photos. She wrote about real people and their real lives. Her writing made you feel so strongly about these people’s stories, just like they were your own. She hoped that through her work the world would understand what really happened in war, and would take action to stop the fighting. On February 22, 2012, the day after she gave her report on the war in Homs, Colvin was killed when the house she was staying in was attacked. She always knew what price a war reporter might have to pay. She already lost an eye before. This time, she gave her life to the work she could not give up — telling the true stories to the world. （註：war 戰爭）

Speaking American is a great book! Lucia Leisure ★★★★★ I just love Josh Katz’s new book! It’s about 42 in different parts of the US. The information in the book was collected from the quiz that Katz built on the website in 2013. The quiz asked what words people use for something, and their answers showed interesting facts. For example, there are different names for sports shoes. In most parts of the US, people say “tennis shoes.” In the northeast of the country, people wear “sneakers.” In some towns, “tennis shoes” and “sneakers” become “gym shoes.”

The use of words tells us where people are from, like Katz’s book says. But in my experience, it also shows 43 . My family has lived in New York since my grandparents. It’s not surprising that I say “sneakers.” But my grandfather says “plimsolls,” and my daughter says “kicks” or “vans.” Maybe Katz can study this difference for his next book.

options.D: worried about

explain:
解題關鍵：校隊贏得全國賽是值得高興與以之為榮的事，固定用法 be proud of 表示「以……為傲」，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：popular with：意為「受……歡迎」，後面通常接喜愛某人的對象，不表示為球隊感到驕傲。
(B)選項原文：proud of：意為「以……為傲」，正好表達大家為校隊獲勝感到光榮。
(C)選項原文：sorry for：意為「為……感到難過、抱歉」，與獲勝的正面情境相反。
(D)選項原文：worried about：意為「擔心……」，題幹沒有令人擔心的訊息。

subject: 英語
stem: Tomorrow is Sam’s last day in the office. Nobody knows why he decided to ___.

options.C: pack
options.D: walk

explain:
解題關鍵：明天是 Sam 在辦公室的最後一天，表示他決定離開這份工作或辦公室；decide to 後接原形動詞 leave，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：hide：意為「躲藏」，最後一天不等於要躲起來。
(B)選項原文：leave：意為「離開」，與 last day in the office 的線索完全相符。
(C)選項原文：pack：意為「打包」，雖可能是離職前的動作，卻不能直接說明最後一天的原因。
(D)選項原文：walk：意為「走路」，與辭職或離開辦公室無關。

subject: 英語
stem: It’s not a good idea to go mountain climbing in this bad ___. We should wait until the typhoon goes away.

options.C: habit
options.D: weather

explain:
解題關鍵：後句提到 typhoon「颱風」尚未離開，題幹談的是不適合登山的惡劣天氣，因此選 weather。
(A)選項原文：chance：意為「機會」，bad chance 不表示颱風天。
(B)選項原文：dream：意為「夢想」，不能因為颱風而說 bad dream。
(C)選項原文：habit：意為「習慣」，與颱風及登山安全沒有關係。
(D)選項原文：weather：意為「天氣」，bad weather 正是指颱風帶來的惡劣天候。

subject: 英語
stem: Chris loves walking with Anna on snowy days, but Anna hates ___ very much.

options.C: one
options.D: it

explain:
解題關鍵：walking with Anna on snowy days 是一件事，Anna 討厭「那件事」時用代名詞 it 代替整個動作片語，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：them：是複數受格代名詞，不能指前面的單一活動。
(B)選項原文：so：意為「如此、所以」，不是可放在 hate 後作受詞的代名詞。
(C)選項原文：one：通常代替一個可數名詞，不能代替 walking 這個活動。
(D)選項原文：it：可代替前述「在下雪天散步」這件事，文法和語意都正確。

subject: 英語
stem: Lora likes to eat bananas that are already a little brown on the outside, and so ___ I.

options.C: have
options.D: will

explain:
解題關鍵：前半句 Lora likes to eat... 是一般現在式的肯定句；so + 助動詞 + 主詞表示「我也是」，要用 do，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：am：只用來呼應 be 動詞，前句的主要動詞是 likes，不可用 am。
(B)選項原文：do：用來代替一般動詞 like，so do I 表示「我也喜歡」，正確。
(C)選項原文：have：用於完成式或 have 當主要動詞，前句不是這兩種情況。
(D)選項原文：will：表示未來，前句在說平常的喜好，時態不合。

subject: 英語
stem: Your refrigerator shouldn’t be making loud noises now, but if it ___ does, just give me a call and I’ll come check it again.

options.C: finally
options.D: still

explain:
解題關鍵：冰箱現在本來不該發出巨響，but if it still does 表示「但如果它仍然這樣」，still 最能承接前後的預期與持續狀態，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：already：意為「已經」，不能表達噪音持續未停止。
(B)選項原文：even：意為「甚至」，需要用來強調意外程度，與句意不合。
(C)選項原文：finally：意為「終於」，表示事情到最後才發生，不是持續發生。
(D)選項原文：still：意為「仍然」，指出冰箱若依舊發出聲響就再通知維修者。

subject: 英語
stem: After winning money in the card game, Jay decided to try again. He felt that he might also be ___ a second time.

options.C: lucky
options.D: ready

explain:
解題關鍵：Jay 先在牌局贏錢，又想再試一次，因為他覺得第二次也可能走運；be lucky 表示「幸運的」，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：famous：意為「有名的」，贏一次錢不表示會變得有名。
(B)選項原文：interested：意為「感興趣的」，不能解釋他期待再次贏錢。
(C)選項原文：lucky：意為「幸運的」，與第一次贏錢、期待再贏的情境相符。
(D)選項原文：ready：意為「準備好的」，雖可說準備再玩，卻不搭配 might also be 來表示運氣。

subject: 英語
stem: The knife doesn’t cut very well. It’s not as ___ as before.

options.C: quick
options.D: sharp

explain:
解題關鍵：刀子切不好，表示刀鋒不夠銳利；as ... as 中間放形容詞 sharp「鋒利的」，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：bright：意為「明亮的」，描述光線或顏色，不描述刀刃切割力。
(B)選項原文：heavy：意為「重的」，重量不是刀子切不好的主要原因。
(C)選項原文：quick：意為「快速的」，不能直接形容刀刃的銳利程度。
(D)選項原文：sharp：意為「鋒利的」，刀不利時就可說 not as sharp as before。

subject: 英語
stem: John will stay with his sister until he ___ an apartment.

options.C: finds
options.D: found

explain:
解題關鍵：until 引導的時間副詞子句，即使主句用未來式 will stay，子句仍用一般現在式表示未來；主詞 he 是第三人稱單數，故用 finds。
(A)選項原文：will find：until 子句不可用 will 表未來，文法不合。
(B)選項原文：would find：表示假設或過去將來，與確定的未來安排不合。
(C)選項原文：finds：一般現在式第三人稱單數，符合 until 子句的規則。
(D)選項原文：found：過去式，題幹說的是未來會暫住到找到房子為止。

subject: 英語
stem: Students ___ to go on the school trip should ask their parents first.

options.C: who they want
options.D: what they want

explain:
解題關鍵：主詞 Students 後需用關係子句修飾「想參加校外旅行的學生」；who 指人，且代替複數 Students，所以動詞用 want，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：who want：who 引導關係子句，want 與複數先行詞 Students 一致，正確。
(B)選項原文：want：少了關係代名詞，Students want to go... 會成為主要句，後面的 should 無法接續。
(C)選項原文：who they want：who 與 they 重複當主詞，且語意變成「他們想要誰」。
(D)選項原文：what they want：what 表示「……的事物」，不能用來修飾前面的 Students。

subject: 英語
stem: The temple sits alone in the mountains at a height of 3,000m ___ sea level.

options.C: below
options.D: in

explain:
解題關鍵：高度的固定說法是 at a height of ... above sea level，表示「海拔……公尺」；寺廟在山上三千公尺海拔，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：above：above sea level 是「高於海平面」，符合海拔高度的用法。
(B)選項原文：at：at sea level 才是「在海平面」，不能接 3,000m 表示海拔。
(C)選項原文：below：below sea level 是「低於海平面」，與山中高處矛盾。
(D)選項原文：in：in sea level 不是正確搭配。

subject: 英語
stem: Patty spent several days planning to invite Charlie to dinner, ___ she couldn’t say a word when they met.

options.C: or
options.D: so

explain:
解題關鍵：Patty 花了好幾天規劃邀請，見面時卻一句話也說不出來，前後是轉折關係，故選 but。
(A)選項原文：but：意為「但是」，連接努力準備與臨場說不出口的反差，正確。
(B)選項原文：if：意為「如果」，會形成條件句，題幹沒有條件關係。
(C)選項原文：or：意為「或者」，用於選擇，不符合前後對比。
(D)選項原文：so：意為「所以」，表示因果；準備多日不會導出不能說話的結果。

subject: 英語
stem: I can’t tell you what I think of the movie because I ___ it. I’ll probably watch it this Saturday.

options.C: haven’t seen
options.D: won’t see

explain:
解題關鍵：說話者現在還不能評論電影，並說週六可能才會看，表示到現在為止尚未看過，應用現在完成式 haven’t seen，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：am not seeing：現在進行式表示正在不看，不能表示「至今沒看過」。
(B)選項原文：don’t see：一般現在式像是在說習慣，不合一次尚未看電影的情境。
(C)選項原文：haven’t seen：現在完成式表示「到現在還沒看過」，與後句週六才看相符。
(D)選項原文：won’t see：未來不會看，和 I’ll probably watch it this Saturday 矛盾。

subject: 英語
stem: The new guy at the help desk answers calls like a ___. There are no ups and downs in his voice and you can’t tell if he is happy or sad.

options.C: radio
options.D: robot

explain:
解題關鍵：題幹說聲音沒有高低起伏，聽不出快樂或難過，像機器人般單調；like a robot 是合理比喻，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：father：意為「父親」，不是形容機械、平板聲音的比喻。
(B)選項原文：foreigner：意為「外國人」，國籍不代表聲音沒有情緒。
(C)選項原文：radio：意為「收音機」，可播放不同聲音，不能準確對應單調語調。
(D)選項原文：robot：意為「機器人」，常用來比喻沒有情緒起伏的說話方式。

subject: 英語
stem: Jasmine planned to spend her summer in the country, but right after she got there, she started to ___ the noise in the city.

options.C: miss
options.D: notice

explain:
解題關鍵：Jasmine 原本要在鄉下過夏天，到了那裡卻開始想念城市的噪音；miss 表示「想念、懷念」，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：enjoy：意為「享受」，若享受鄉下生活，不會用 but 表示反差。
(B)選項原文：mind：意為「介意」，開始介意城市的噪音不合她人在鄉下的情境。
(C)選項原文：miss：意為「想念」，說明她離開城市後反而懷念城市的聲音。
(D)選項原文：notice：意為「注意到」，人不在城市時不能因到鄉下才注意到城市噪音。

subject: 英語
stem: “Bad traffic” is perhaps the ___ excuse for being late when your boss knows it only takes you five minutes to walk to work.

options.C: smartest
options.D: worst

explain:
解題關鍵：走到公司只要五分鐘，卻用「塞車」當遲到理由，老闆一定不信，這是最糟的藉口；the worst excuse 符合語意，故選 D。
(A)選項原文：easiest：意為「最容易的」，不評價藉口是否可信。
(B)選項原文：oldest：意為「最老的」，不合比較藉口好壞的語境。
(C)選項原文：smartest：意為「最聰明的」，明知只要走五分鐘還說塞車，反而不聰明。
(D)選項原文：worst：意為「最糟的」，與這個明顯站不住腳的遲到藉口相符。

subject: 英語
stem: The housework in Mr. and Mrs. Wang’s family ___ between them and their kids. Everyone’s got their own job to do.

options.C: shares
options.D: share

explain:
解題關鍵：家事是被家人分配、共同承擔的事，需用被動語態；housework 是不可數名詞，視為單數，故用 is shared。
(A)選項原文：is shared：單數 be 動詞加過去分詞，表示「家事被分攤」，正確。
(B)選項原文：are shared：are 搭配複數主詞，但 housework 是不可數單數概念。
(C)選項原文：shares：主動語態，會變成「家事分攤」，缺少被分攤的受事關係。
(D)選項原文：share：主動原形動詞，既缺主詞一致也不符被動意思。

subject: 英語
stem: I want to find another dentist because ___ pulled out a good tooth last time I went to him.

options.C: mine
options.D: myself

explain:
解題關鍵：說話者要換牙醫，因為「我的那一位」上次拔掉好牙；mine 是名詞性所有代名詞，可單獨代替 my dentist，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：I：主格代名詞，放在 because 後會變成自己拔牙，語意錯誤。
(B)選項原文：me：受格代名詞，不能作 pulled out 的主詞。
(C)選項原文：mine：可代替 my dentist，意為「我的牙醫」，且可獨立作主詞。
(D)選項原文：myself：反身代名詞，指「我自己」，不是「我的牙醫」。

subject: 英語
stem: Mom: Linda, you’ve been playing computer games all evening! Have you finished your report? Linda: Well, ___ most of it this afternoon, and I’ll finish it by Friday.

options.C: I was doing
options.D: I’ll do

explain:
解題關鍵：Linda 說「今天下午已經做了大部分」，是在晚上回顧已完成的動作，應用一般過去式 I did；剩下的才在週五前完成，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：I would do：表示假設或過去將來，沒有交代條件，不合對話。
(B)選項原文：I did：一般過去式，指出下午確實完成大部分報告，正確。
(C)選項原文：I was doing：表示下午某一時刻正在做，不能清楚表示已完成大部分。
(D)選項原文：I’ll do：表示未來要做，與 this afternoon 的過去時間矛盾。

subject: 英語
stem: Why did Philip go out?

options.C: To ask the police for help.
options.D: To buy food for his brother.

explain:
解題關鍵：文章明說 Jason 肚子餓又一直哭，Philip 不會煮飯，於是決定帶 Jason 出去買食物，因此選 D。
(A)選項原文：To meet a woman.：文章中的女子是回家後才看見的，Philip 出門前不認識她。
(B)選項原文：To look for his father.：父親在辦公室加班，文中沒有說 Philip 外出找父親。
(C)選項原文：To ask the police for help.：警察是在他們回家後才出現，並非出門目的。
(D)選項原文：To buy food for his brother.：Jason 很餓，Philip 帶他出去找食物，直接符合文章證據。
passage: It was around eight o’clock on Saturday night. Philip was at home with his little brother, Jason. Jason was hungry and kept crying. But Philip couldn’t cook and their father was not home yet because he was working late in the office. So Philip decided to take Jason out for some food. Half an hour later, when they came back home, Philip was surprised to find that their father was talking to the police and a woman outside their house. He didn’t know who the woman was. She looked scared and stood behind the police. Philip’s father was very angry and kept shouting, “I didn’t do anything wrong! I forgot my keys and was just trying to get into MY OWN HOUSE!” But the police didn’t believe him until Philip ran to them and explained everything. The police told Philip that the woman called 110 when she saw Philip’s father trying to get into a house through a window. That was how it all happened.
group_title: 第22–23題題組

subject: 英語
stem: Why was Philip’s father angry?

options.B: The woman was hiding from him.
options.C: The police didn’t believe what he said.
options.D: Philip and his brother went out at night.

explain:
解題關鍵：父親一邊喊「I didn’t do anything wrong!」並說自己忘了鑰匙、正要進自己的房子；文章接著說警察直到 Philip 解釋才相信，故他生氣是因警察不信他。
(A)選項原文：He forgot his keys.：忘記鑰匙是事情的起因之一，但不是文中父親大喊、生氣的直接原因。
(B)選項原文：The woman was hiding from him.：女子是害怕地站在警察後面，文章沒說她躲父親。
(C)選項原文：The police didn’t believe what he said.：警察起初不相信他在進自己的家，完全符合文本。
(D)選項原文：Philip and his brother went out at night.：兄弟外出不是父親對警察發怒的原因。
passage: It was around eight o’clock on Saturday night. Philip was at home with his little brother, Jason. Jason was hungry and kept crying. But Philip couldn’t cook and their father was not home yet because he was working late in the office. So Philip decided to take Jason out for some food. Half an hour later, when they came back home, Philip was surprised to find that their father was talking to the police and a woman outside their house. He didn’t know who the woman was. She looked scared and stood behind the police. Philip’s father was very angry and kept shouting, “I didn’t do anything wrong! I forgot my keys and was just trying to get into MY OWN HOUSE!” But the police didn’t believe him until Philip ran to them and explained everything. The police told Philip that the woman called 110 when she saw Philip’s father trying to get into a house through a window. That was how it all happened.
group_title: 第22–23題題組

subject: 英語
stem: Kevin is going to buy some fresh bread at Baker’s Kitchen. He loves white bread, his mom likes farm bread, his father enjoys bagels, and his sister eats only challah. Which is the earliest possible time for him to get all these breads for his family?
explain:
解題關鍵：圖表顯示白麵包 10:30am、bagels 11:30am、challah 3:30pm、farm bread 4:30pm 出爐；要一次買到四種新鮮麵包，必須等最晚的 farm bread，5:00pm 是最早可行時間，故選 C。
(A)選項原文：11:00am.：此時 bagels、challah、farm bread 都尚未出爐。
(B)選項原文：4:00pm.：farm bread 要到 4:30pm 才有，時間太早。
(C)選項原文：5:00pm.：四種麵包在此之前都已出爐，是最早符合條件的選項。
(D)選項原文：7:00pm.：也買得到，但比 5:00pm 晚，不是 earliest possible time。
passage: （註：oven 烤爐）
group_title: 第24–25題題組

subject: 英語
stem: What do we know about Baker’s Kitchen?

options.A: It is open five days a week.
options.B: Its breads are half price one hour before closing.
options.C: Its croissants and pretzels are sold on weekends.
options.D: Its members can save $100 when they shop on Fridays.

explain:
解題關鍵：圖表寫著「All breads at half price after 8pm (after 7pm on Saturdays and Sundays)」；平日 9pm 關門、週末 8pm 關門，都是關門前一小時後半價，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：It is open five days a week.：營業時間包含 Mon. to Fri. 與 Sat. & Sun.，一週開七天。
(B)選項原文：Its breads are half price one hour before closing.：平日八點後、週末七點後半價，皆為關門前一小時，正確。
(C)選項原文：Its croissants and pretzels are sold on weekends.：圖上標示 croissants 和 pretzels 都是 Friday only，不是週末。
(D)選項原文：Its members can save $100 when they shop on Fridays.：會員費是 $100，折扣是所有消費省 10%，並非週五省 $100。
passage: （註：oven 烤爐）
group_title: 第24–25題題組

subject: 英語
stem: What is recommended to people who want to visit the festival? （註：recommend 推薦 ）

options.A: Using the free festival bus service.
options.B: Visiting the festival on the weekend.
options.C: Entering Satyr’s Park from Fox Street.
options.D: Parking in Garden Square and walking to the festival.

explain:
解題關鍵：公告第 2 點直接寫「You are welcome to take the Free Festival Bus at the Goat Street Station」，明確推薦遊客搭免費節慶巴士，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：Using the free festival bus service.：這是公告直接歡迎遊客使用的服務，正確。

subject: 英語
stem: What kind of people do Yan’s and Chang’s friends most likely think （註：likely 可能 Yan and Chang are? ）

options.C: They like to make friends.
options.D: They don’t like new things.

explain:
解題關鍵：Yan 只請客人吃一條小魚；Chang 明明養很多鴨和雞卻不留朋友吃午飯。兩位朋友用反諷提醒主人不肯分享，因此選 B。
(A)選項原文：They enjoy good food.：文章沒有說 Yan 或 Chang 喜愛美食，重點是他們給得太少。
(B)選項原文：They don’t like to share.：兩人都有食物卻不願招待朋友，最符合兩則故事。
(C)選項原文：They like to make friends.：邀請或接待朋友不等於喜歡交新朋友，且文中焦點在吝嗇。
(D)選項原文：They don’t like new things.：故事沒有談到新事物。
passage:
Yan lived a good life in a big house. One day he invited a friend to dinner at his house. However, on the dinner table there was only one small dish of one small fish. The friend looked quietly at the fish. It was no bigger than a finger. Then he asked Yan if he could borrow a lamp. “What for?” Yan asked. “Well, it’s so dark in here,” the friend said with a dry smile, “I can’t see the other delicious dishes you’ve prepared for me.”

Chang kept a lot of ducks and chickens on his farm. One day, his best friend came to visit him. At noon, Chang told his friend that he couldn’t let him stay for lunch because there wasn’t much food to eat. The friend looked out at Chang’s farm animals for a moment. Then he asked Chang if he had a big knife. “Yes, but what for?” Chang asked. “I’m thinking about killing the horse I rode here so we’ll have something for lunch,” the friend said. “But how are you going to go home without it?” “Well, you wouldn’t mind lending me one of your many ducks or chickens so I can ride it home, would you?”

subject: 英語
stem: Why does the writer talk about doctors and a health center in the reading?

options.B: To talk about Chen’s future plans.
options.C: To explain Chen’s love for books.
options.D: To show why bookstores are important.

explain:
解題關鍵：文章用醫院比喻大圖書館和博物館修嚴重的舊書，用健康中心比喻 Chen 修一般民眾有小問題的書；這是在說明他提供的修書服務，故選 A。
(A)選項原文：To explain Chen’s services.：醫師、醫院與健康中心的比喻清楚比較他的修書工作內容，正確。
(B)選項原文：To talk about Chen’s future plans.：文章沒有描述他未來要做的計畫。
(C)選項原文：To explain Chen’s love for books.：他關心書籍可推知喜愛，但比喻主要在解釋服務分工。
(D)選項原文：To show why bookstores are important.：重點是修復書籍，不是證明所有書店的重要性。
passage: Usually, people visit bookstores to buy books. But those who walk into Cotoha come to see its owner, Chen Bing-Hong. They bring him books with different problems. Some have lost their covers, some are missing a few pages, and some have pages that are falling out. Chen can always fix the books and make them whole again. Chen sees himself as a doctor. He says that books, like people, get sick and need help. In Taiwan, there are not many “doctors” like him, and most of them work for big libraries and museums. If big libraries and museums are hospitals, Chen’s bookstore is a health center. Big libraries and museums fix important old books with serious problems, and Chen helps people with books that have smaller problems. However, the smaller size of the problems doesn’t mean Chen’s job is less important. Chen gave an example of a science book he once worked on. It was very old and half of its cover was lost. Its owner still wanted to keep it because it was a gift from a teacher who helped him follow his dream of studying science. When he got his book back, he was very surprised at the new-old book. He felt he was brought back to the days with his teacher. Seeing the owner’s smile made Chen happy, because smiles like that are what his magic is for.

subject: 英語
stem: According to the reading, why did Rohla and Kreytenberg open Habibi & Hawara?

options.A: To help refugees live better in Austria.
options.B: To collect money to help Syria fight the war.
options.C: To help Austrians learn about the war in Syria.
options.D: To help refugees go back to their home countries.

explain:
解題關鍵：兩位創辦人認為難民不必是問題，想幫他們展開新生活，便讓曾在敘利亞當廚師的難民有工作，因此開店的目的在幫難民在奧地利過得更好，選 A。
(A)選項原文：To help refugees live better in Austria.：提供工作並幫助難民開始新生活，正是文章主旨。
(B)選項原文：To collect money to help Syria fight the war.：店家沒有募款或支援戰爭的計畫。
(C)選項原文：To help Austrians learn about the war in Syria.：文章談民眾對難民的擔心，不是以戰爭教育為目的。
(D)選項原文：To help refugees go back to their home countries.：他們要協助難民在奧地利開始生活，不是送回原國。
passage:
A Delicious Surprise and Welcome Change By Karl Falk, June 1, 2016

In Austria, there are not many restaurants like Habibi & Hawara. Here you can enjoy Austrian and Syrian food together. Two Austrians, Martin Rohla and David Kreytenberg, started this yummy plan from their experience of working with refugees.

Every year, thousands of people have to leave their homes and families because of war in their countries. So many of them go to Austria that some people in the country think they have become a problem. They are afraid refugees may take away their jobs and they don’t feel safe around them, either. But Rohla and Kreytenberg would beg to differ: The refugees don’t have to be a problem. They want to help them start a new life. They invited refugees to meetings and found that some of them were cooks back in Syria. So the idea of Habibi & Hawara was born—a restaurant that brings together Austrian and Syrian food. “The two worlds far away from each other meet together,” Kreytenberg said.

But Rohla and Kreytenberg want to do more than just give the refugees work. They want their best workers to buy the restaurant in the end. They hope that Habibi & Hawara is not just a one-time plan and that other Austrians will join them and help more refugees.

（註：refugee 難民 war 戰爭）

subject: 英語
stem: What does it mean when someone is an advocate of something?

options.A: They talk a lot but do little about it.
options.B: They believe it is good and should be done.
options.C: They have had some bad experiences with it.
options.D: They are one of the first people who have done it.

explain:
解題關鍵：Smith 主張人類弄髒動物棲地，且「must do everything we can to bring them back」；可知 an advocate of 是支持並主張應實行某事的人，故選 B。
(A)選項原文：They talk a lot but do little about it.：文章沒有批評 Smith 只說不做。
(B)選項原文：They believe it is good and should be done.：Smith 認為應盡力復育絕種動物，正是倡議者的意思。
(C)選項原文：They have had some bad experiences with it.：有壞經驗不是 advocate 的定義。
(D)選項原文：They are one of the first people who have done it.：先做某事的人不一定支持或提倡它。
passage:
VOICES OF PEOPLE If you want to learn about bringing back extinct animals, reading John Smith’s Back from the Dead is a good start. But I have to say I can’t agree with everything he says. Ellen Zimmer

From his book, I can see Smith is an advocate of bringing extinct animals back. He says we have lost many animals because we made their living spaces too dirty. He also thinks we must do everything we can to bring them back. However, I don’t know how much time and money we would need to make the world a better place for them, and honestly no one knows if they could actually come back.

Smith also says that bringing back extinct animals may be good for us. He talks about an extinct frog that grew tadpoles in its stomach. Some women’s babies die before they are born, and Smith believes bringing back the frog may be an answer to the problem. According to him, by studying how the tadpoles grow inside the frog’s stomach, we might be able to find new ways to help these women successfully keep their babies. But I don’t think things are as easy as Smith thinks. We have spent ten years and millions of dollars on this kind of frog, but all we have got are only a few dead frog eggs. If we can’t see a real frog, how can we be sure women will get the help they need?

Dr. Solomon Wang from the Animal Saving Office says the study of bringing back extinct animals is “throwing good money after bad.” And he’s right. A lot of hard work has been put into this expensive dream, but we haven’t seen anything come out of it. So should we still keep going down this road?

（註：extinct 絕種的 tadpole 蝌蚪）

subject: 英語
stem: Why does Ellen Zimmer use the words from Dr. Solomon Wang?

options.C: To make her idea clearer.
options.D: To invite people to take action.

explain:
解題關鍵：Ellen 先質疑投入十年、數百萬美元卻只得到幾顆死蛙卵，接著引用 Wang 的「throwing good money after bad」並說 he’s right，是用專家話語強化自己認為不值得繼續投資的觀點，故選 C。

(B)選項原文：To share a big dream.：Wang 的話批評昂貴夢想，不是在分享夢想。
(C)選項原文：To make her idea clearer.：引用精確說出她「投入很多卻沒有成果」的反對理由，正確。
(D)選項原文：To invite people to take action.：她提出疑問，沒有號召讀者採取行動。

VOICES OF PEOPLE If you want to learn about bringing back extinct animals, reading John Smith’s Back from the Dead is a good start. But I have to say I can’t agree with everything he says. Ellen Zimmer

From his book, I can see Smith is an advocate of bringing extinct animals back. He says we have lost many animals because we made their living spaces too dirty. He also thinks we must do everything we can to bring them back. However, I don’t know how much time and money we would need to make the world a better place for them, and honestly no one knows if they could actually come back.

Smith also says that bringing back extinct animals may be good for us. He talks about an extinct frog that grew tadpoles in its stomach. Some women’s babies die before they are born, and Smith believes bringing back the frog may be an answer to the problem. According to him, by studying how the tadpoles grow inside the frog’s stomach, we might be able to find new ways to help these women successfully keep their babies. But I don’t think things are as easy as Smith thinks. We have spent ten years and millions of dollars on this kind of frog, but all we have got are only a few dead frog eggs. If we can’t see a real frog, how can we be sure women will get the help they need?

Dr. Solomon Wang from the Animal Saving Office says the study of bringing back extinct animals is “throwing good money after bad.” And he’s right. A lot of hard work has been put into this expensive dream, but we haven’t seen anything come out of it. So should we still keep going down this road?

（註：extinct 絕種的 tadpole 蝌蚪）

A HISTORY LESSON ON THE PANDEMIC 2020.10.29

Since the Covid-19 pandemic started, people have begun “social distancing”— keeping a safe space between you and anyone you don’t live with. Though it has been a very popular topic this year, social distancing 40 . In fact, it was widely used in the U.S. in the flu pandemic in 1918. But how well did it work? The Americans’ experience can tell us whether it really saved lives.

From the picture, we can see that 41 started social distancing earlier than the other three cities. This helped the city keep the number of deaths down. Besides taking early action, keeping the action long enough was also important in fighting the pandemic. The picture shows that Portland and Denver did well in the first few weeks. However, both cities 42 , and the numbers of deaths climbed again. But there was one thing Portland did right. The city used several ways of social distancing at the same time to deal with the pandemic. 43 , sick people were kept away from healthy ones; schools were closed; public activities were not allowed. All these were useful in keeping people safe. The lessons of the 1918 pandemic bring us hope. While we are still learning to fight Covid-19, social distancing may be the best way to get us through the dark days, at least for now.

(A)選項原文：bird 是鳥；圖中雖有小鳥，但題幹的單數 a 搭配畫面中飛越房屋的主要大型飛行器，不是牠。
(B)選項原文：butterfly 是蝴蝶；牠在花叢附近飛，不是在房屋上空的那一個。
(C)選項原文：kite 是風箏；畫面左側有人放風箏，但題目所指的高空飛行器沒有線牽著。

subject: 英語
stem: When I was a teenager, I was very ___. But now, it’s easier for me to talk to people.

options.C: popular
options.D: shy

explain:
解題關鍵：But now 表示與青少年時期形成對比；現在較容易和人說話，推知以前不敢或不擅長主動交談，應是 shy（害羞的），選 D。
(A)選項原文：happy 是快樂的，不能合理說明以前不容易與人交談。
(B)選項原文：lazy 是懶惰的，與說話是否自在沒有直接關係。
(C)選項原文：popular 是受歡迎的；受歡迎不等於不敢開口，且和後句轉折不合。
(D)選項原文：shy 是害羞的；害羞的人常不易和陌生人交談，最符合前後對比。

subject: 英語
stem: Lena doesn’t want to go ___ with John because she is afraid of water.

options.C: sailing
options.D: shopping

explain:
解題關鍵：because she is afraid of water 說明 Lena 害怕水，因此不想從事需要在水上的 sailing（航行、划船），選 C。
(A)選項原文：dancing 是跳舞，通常不必接觸水，不能由怕水推得。
(B)選項原文：hiking 是健行，主要在陸地上進行。
(C)選項原文：sailing 是駕船航行；活動在水上，正是她害怕而不想去的事。
(D)選項原文：shopping 是購物，與水沒有必然關係。

subject: 英語
stem: Cindy enjoys ___ her dad read stories to her before bed.

options.C: listen to
options.D: listens to

explain:
解題關鍵：enjoy 後面要接 V-ing，表示享受做某事；listen to her dad read stories 是聽爸爸讀故事，所以應填 listening to，選 B。
(A)選項原文：to listen to 是不定詞；enjoy 不接 to V，文法不符。
(B)選項原文：listening to 是動名詞片語，符合 enjoy + V-ing 的句型，為標準答案。
(C)選項原文：listen to 是原形動詞；前面已有 enjoys，不能直接接原形。
(D)選項原文：listens to 是第三人稱單數動詞；enjoys 後不能再接另一個限定動詞。

subject: 英語
stem: Dad is busy cooking in the kitchen. Dinner will be ___ in ten minutes.

options.C: medium
options.D: ready

explain:
解題關鍵：爸爸正在煮晚餐，in ten minutes 表示十分鐘後就能吃了；be ready 意為準備好，選 D。
(A)選項原文：free 是免費的或空閒的，不能形容晚餐完成可上桌。
(B)選項原文：full 是飽的或滿的，不表示食物煮好了。
(C)選項原文：medium 是中等的，常用於程度或熟度，不能放在此處表示完成。
(D)選項原文：ready 是準備好的，符合晚餐十分鐘後完成的情境。

subject: 英語
stem: There are so many new ___ in the office. It’ll take me some time to remember who is who.

options.C: rules
options.D: tools

explain:
解題關鍵：who is who 是要辨認每一個人；new faces 可指新來的人或新面孔，因此選 A。
(A)選項原文：faces 是臉、面孔；new faces 在此指辦公室有許多新同事，最合語意。
(B)選項原文：ideas 是想法，無法用 who is who 來辨認。
(C)選項原文：rules 是規則，需要記內容而不是記誰是誰。
(D)選項原文：tools 是工具，不會對應到 who。

subject: 英語
stem: I feel like a ___. I was looking for my keys for hours but they have been in my pocket the whole time.

options.C: king
options.D: stranger

explain:
解題關鍵：鑰匙一直在自己口袋裡，卻找了好幾個小時，說話者責怪自己粗心，feel like a fool 是覺得自己像傻瓜，選 A。
(A)選項原文：fool 是傻瓜；最能表達發現真相後的自嘲。
(B)選項原文：ghost 是鬼，與找不到其實在口袋裡的鑰匙無關。
(C)選項原文：king 是國王，沒有自責或粗心的意思。
(D)選項原文：stranger 是陌生人，不能描述自己做了糊塗事的感受。

subject: 英語
stem: Mr. and Mrs. Wu have three daughters. Two are in high school, and ___ is in elementary school.

options.C: the one
options.D: the next

explain:
解題關鍵：共有三個女兒，前句已指出其中兩位在高中，剩下的是特定的一位；the other 可指其餘那一個，選 B。
(A)選項原文：each 是每一個，後面通常接單數名詞或用於 each of，不能指明剩下那一位。
(B)選項原文：the other 是另外那一個；用來指三人中已提兩人後的最後一人，正確。
(C)選項原文：the one 需有明確對比或後置修飾，單獨放在此處不能表達其餘一人。
(D)選項原文：the next 是下一個，帶有順序意義，題幹沒有排序。

subject: 英語
stem: It is hard for trees to ___ along this beach because of the strong winds from the sea.

options.C: follow
options.D: grow

explain:
解題關鍵：海邊強風會使植物不易生長；trees grow 是樹木生長，選 D。
(A)選項原文：blow 是吹；風會吹，不是樹木自己 blow。
(B)選項原文：build 是建造；樹木不會建造東西。
(C)選項原文：follow 是跟隨；與強風造成的植物生存困難無關。
(D)選項原文：grow 是生長；符合強風不利樹木生長的因果關係。

subject: 英語
stem: Christmas ___ and I want to visit my aunt abroad. Do you have any plans yet?

options.C: is coming
options.D: was coming

explain:
解題關鍵：說話者正在討論尚未到的聖誕節與旅行計畫，現在進行式 is coming 可表示即將發生的事，選 C。
(A)選項原文：came 是過去式，表示聖誕節已到過，和 yet 詢問未來計畫矛盾。
(B)選項原文：comes 是現在簡單式，較適合固定事實或習慣，不如 is coming 能表達即將到來。
(C)選項原文：is coming 是現在進行式表近期未來，與旅行計畫的語境相符。
(D)選項原文：was coming 是過去進行式，需有過去時間背景，題幹沒有。

subject: 英語
stem: Jo won’t be happy if you’re late for his party tonight, so ___ sure that you arrive on time.

options.C: to make
options.D: is making

explain:
解題關鍵：so 後是在給對方提醒：務必準時到；祈使句以原形動詞開頭，固定用法為 make sure that...，選 A。
(A)選項原文：make 是原形動詞，可形成祈使句 Make sure that...，為標準答案。
(B)選項原文：makes 是第三人稱單數動詞；祈使句沒有這樣的主詞，不可用。
(C)選項原文：to make 是不定詞；so 後此處不是要接目的不定詞。
(D)選項原文：is making 是進行式，需有主詞，且不符合提醒的語氣。

subject: 英語
stem: You may have a long drive because of the terrible ___. There are usually a lot of cars and buses during this time.

options.C: service
options.D: traffic

explain:
解題關鍵：許多汽車和公車會造成塞車，使開車時間變長；terrible traffic 是糟糕的交通狀況，選 D。
(A)選項原文：experience 是經驗或經歷，不能指道路上的車流。
(B)選項原文：machine 是機器，題幹說的是許多車輛造成的狀況。
(C)選項原文：service 是服務，沒有塞車的意思。
(D)選項原文：traffic 是交通、車流；可解釋為何車程會拉長。

subject: 英語
stem: In the future, there will ___ be greater basketball players than Stephen Curry, but now we believe he is the best!

options.C: never
options.D: perhaps

explain:
解題關鍵：未來是否會出現更偉大的球員無法確定，因此要用 perhaps（也許）；but now 表示目前仍相信 Curry 最好，選 D。
(A)選項原文：again 是再次，不能表達對未來可能性的保留。
(B)選項原文：already 是已經，與 In the future 的時間概念衝突。
(C)選項原文：never 是絕不；語氣過度絕對，和未來未知不合。
(D)選項原文：perhaps 是也許，恰能表達未來可能有人更出色。

subject: 英語
stem: I guess the rainwater has come in from the kitchen. See? ___ of the windows are closed except the one in the kitchen.

options.C: Most
options.D: Some

explain:
解題關鍵：except the one in the kitchen 表示廚房那一扇是唯一沒關的窗，其他窗全關了；all of the windows 是全部的窗戶，選 A。
(A)選項原文：All 是全部；All of the windows are closed except... 正確表達只有一扇例外。
(B)選項原文：Both 只用於兩個；題幹是 windows，未限定只有兩扇。
(C)選項原文：Most 是大多數；若用 most，仍可能有不只一扇窗未關，和 except the one 不符。
(D)選項原文：Some 是一些，無法表達其他窗都關著。

subject: 英語
stem: ___ machines have been used to pick fruits for a long time, they were not used on strawberry farms until several years ago.

options.C: Before
options.D: If

explain:
解題關鍵：採果機器已使用很久，草莓園卻直到幾年前才使用，前後有明顯的讓步轉折，要用 Although，選 A。
(A)選項原文：Although 是雖然；可連接雖然早已存在、但草莓園晚用的對比，正確。
(B)選項原文：Because 是因為；兩句不是因果，而是出乎預期的對照。
(C)選項原文：Before 是在……之前；接完整子句後無法表達此處的轉折關係。
(D)選項原文：If 是如果；題幹敘述既成事實，不是條件假設。

subject: 英語
stem: There are online videos that teach you exercises you can do at home. They’ll ___ you a trip to the gym, and some money too.

options.C: keep
options.D: save

explain:
解題關鍵：影片教人在家運動，就不必跑一趟健身房，也少花一些錢；save 人 time、money 或 a trip 表示替人省下，選 D。
(A)選項原文：cost 是花費；在家運動應減少花費，不會 cost you a trip。
(B)選項原文：give 是給；影片不會給你一趟去健身房的路程。
(C)選項原文：keep 是保留，不能和 a trip、some money 構成此意。
(D)選項原文：save 是省下；可同時搭配 a trip to the gym 和 some money。

subject: 英語
stem: Jane’s parents are always happy to see their grandchildren, but mine ___ less so when I visit them with my kids.

options.C: do
options.D: does

explain:
解題關鍵：mine 代替 my parents，是複數；less so 省略 happy，因此要用複數 be 動詞 are，選 B。
(A)選項原文：is 是單數 be 動詞，與 mine 所指的 parents 複數不一致。
(B)選項原文：are 是複數 be 動詞；mine are less so = 我的父母比較不那麼高興，正確。
(C)選項原文：do 是助動詞，後面不能直接接形容詞片語 less so。
(D)選項原文：does 是單數助動詞，既與複數不合，也不能連接 less so。

subject: 英語
stem: Before she ___ about it, you should tell Daphne you broke her favorite cup.

options.C: was asking
options.D: will ask

explain:
解題關鍵：主句有 should tell，指現在起應在未來某事發生前告訴她；before 引導未來時間子句時，英文用現在簡單式代替未來式，she 要搭配 asks，選 A。
(A)選項原文：asks 是現在簡單式第三人稱單數，符合 Before she asks... 的時間子句規則。
(B)選項原文：asked 是過去式，會變成她已經問過，和 should tell 的未來提醒不合。
(C)選項原文：was asking 是過去進行式，需要過去情境，題幹沒有。
(D)選項原文：will ask 雖有未來意義，但 before 時間子句不可用 will。

subject: 英語
stem: It was very windy this morning. Some of the shirts on the balcony were blown away ___ in the pond.

options.C: fallen
options.D: and fallen

explain:
解題關鍵：衣服先 were blown away，接著 fell in the pond；兩個過去動作需用 and 連接，fell 用過去式，選 B。
(A)選項原文：fell 雖是正確過去式，但前面少了連接詞，兩個動詞片語直接相接不通。
(B)選項原文：and fell 用 and 連接兩個過去動作，句子完整，為標準答案。
(C)選項原文：fallen 是過去分詞，不能單獨作本句的主要動詞。
(D)選項原文：and fallen 仍是過去分詞，and 後需與 were blown away 平行的過去式 fell。

subject: 英語
stem: What happened to Rex?

options.C: He bit people.
options.D: He ate too much.

explain:
解題關鍵：文章明說 Rex was hit by a car last night，並且在醫院；被車撞又住院可知牠受傷了，選 B。
(A)選項原文：He got lost. 是牠走失了；文章沒有說 Rex 失蹤，而是說牠在醫院。
(B)選項原文：He got hurt. 是牠受傷了；被車撞正是直接證據，為標準答案。
(C)選項原文：He bit people. 是牠咬人；文章反而說 Rex cute and friendly，沒有咬人情節。
(D)選項原文：He ate too much. 是牠吃太多；文中未提飲食問題，住院原因是車禍。
passage: Rex is a dog that lives at the bakery next to our school. He is cute and friendly. Every morning, he stands in front of the school to welcome everybody. We all see Rex as one of us. But one Monday morning, I was surprised that Rex was not there to say hello to us. ‘Rex is in the hospital. He was hit by a car last night,’ my classmate told me. We went to see Rex in the hospital that day after school. Two weeks later, Rex was much better, and we decided to take him for a walk every evening. Because of the exercise, Rex became healthier and stronger. Soon he could happily run and jump again. He is now as handsome and strong as before!
group_title: 故事：校犬 Rex 康復記

subject: 英語
stem: How did the writer help Rex?

options.C: By taking him to see a doctor.
options.D: By looking for a new home for him.

explain:
解題關鍵：Rex 好轉兩週後，作者和同學決定每天傍晚帶牠散步；文章接著說 Because of the exercise, Rex became healthier and stronger，所以選 B。
(A)選項原文：By calling the police. 是打電話報警；文章沒有提到警方。
(B)選項原文：By making him exercise. 是讓牠運動；每天散步及牠因運動變強壯，就是文本證據。
(C)選項原文：By taking him to see a doctor. 是帶牠看醫生；作者放學後去醫院探望，不是帶牠去就醫。
(D)選項原文：By looking for a new home for him. 是替牠找新家；Rex 一直住在學校旁的麵包店，文中沒有這件事。

But one Monday morning, I was surprised that Rex was not there to say hello to us. ‘Rex is in the hospital. He was hit by a car last night,’ my classmate told me. We went to see Rex in the hospital that day after school. Two weeks later, Rex was much better, and we decided to take him for a walk every evening. Because of the exercise, Rex became healthier and stronger. Soon he could happily run and jump again. He is now as handsome and strong as before!

subject: 英語
stem: What do we know about Mark from the dialogue?

options.B: He is looking for a new job.
options.C: He did not like Linda’s cake.
options.D: He is getting married to Jenny.

explain:
解題關鍵：Jenny 宣布婚訊時，Mark立刻搶著說自己的工作；Linda 說 Come on, Mark，又在最後以 MARK!! 制止他，顯示 Mark 讓 Linda 不高興，選 A。
(A)選項原文：He made Linda unhappy. 是他使 Linda 不高興；Linda 的責備與大寫叫喊就是證據。
(B)選項原文：He is looking for a new job. 是他正在找新工作；他說自己剛得到很想要的工作，並非正在找。
(C)選項原文：He did not like Linda’s cake. 是他不喜歡 Linda 的蛋糕；對話只說他曾插話談自己的巧克力蛋糕，未說不喜歡她的。
(D)選項原文：He is getting married to Jenny. 是他要和 Jenny 結婚；是 Jenny 說自己明年結婚，沒有說對象是 Mark。
passage:
Jenny: Hey guys, guess what? I’m getting married next year!

Linda: Wow, I’m so happy for you.

Mark: I have good news too! I just got the job I’ve wanted so much.

Linda: Come on, Mark. Don’t start again. You’re stealing Jenny’s thunder. Jenny was telling us about her big news. It’s very important to her. And you want us to hear about your new job now?

Mark: I didn’t mean that. I just…

Jenny: I agree. Last time when we were talking about how delicious Linda’s cake was, you started telling us about the chocolate cake you made at home.

Mark: All right, all right, my problem. Sorry, Jenny. I’ll never do that again. So do you want to know what job I got?

Linda: MARK!!
group_title: 群組對話：steal someone’s thunder

subject: 英語
stem: Which is most likely an example of stealing someone’s thunder?

options.A: Dennis never changes his mind except when his wife tells him to.
options.B: Melisa tells Tom she’ll go to the party but tells her mom she’ll stay home.
options.C: Jeff tells everyone he’ll move abroad when Ivy is still telling them about her baby.
options.D: Alisa says she doesn’t care what we have for lunch but also doesn’t like the restaurant we chose.

explain:
解題關鍵：對話中 Linda 解釋 stealing Jenny’s thunder 是 Jenny 正分享重要消息，Mark 卻把大家注意力拉到自己的好消息；C 正是同樣的搶焦點行為，選 C。
(A)選項原文：Dennis never changes his mind except when his wife tells him to. 是 Dennis 只聽妻子的話，沒有搶走他人的注意力。
(B)選項原文：Melisa tells Tom she’ll go to the party but tells her mom she’ll stay home. 是對不同人說不同話，屬於前後不一致。
(C)選項原文：Jeff tells everyone he’ll move abroad when Ivy is still telling them about her baby. 是 Ivy 分享寶寶時 Jeff 突然宣布出國，完全符合搶走別人風采。
(D)選項原文：Alisa says she doesn’t care what we have for lunch but also doesn’t like the restaurant we chose. 是嘴上說不在意、實際挑剔，並未搶話題。

Jenny: Hey guys, guess what? I’m getting married next year!

Linda: Wow, I’m so happy for you.

Mark: I have good news too! I just got the job I’ve wanted so much.

Linda: Come on, Mark. Don’t start again. You’re stealing Jenny’s thunder. Jenny was telling us about her big news. It’s very important to her. And you want us to hear about your new job now?

Mark: I didn’t mean that. I just…

Jenny: I agree. Last time when we were talking about how delicious Linda’s cake was, you started telling us about the chocolate cake you made at home.

Mark: All right, all right, my problem. Sorry, Jenny. I’ll never do that again. So do you want to know what job I got?

Linda: MARK!!
