subject: 英語
stem: What can you do with a White Lake City Card?

options.B: Visit any public museum in the city for free.
options.C: Take a train to places out of the three zones.
options.D: Move around the city by metro as much as you want.

explain:
解題關鍵：圖表第一點寫明持卡可 by metro, bus, or train as many times as you want，故可不限次搭地鐵在市內移動，選 D。
(A)選項原文：Save 20% on children’s train tickets. 是兒童火車票打八折；圖表是可免費帶一名12歲以下兒童，20%折扣則是博物館門票。
(B)選項原文：Visit any public museum in the city for free. 是博物館免費；圖表只說博物館票價省20%，不是免費。
(C)選項原文：Take a train to places out of the three zones. 是可去三區以外；註記明說 Cards are only for trips inside the three zones。
(D)選項原文：Move around the city by metro as much as you want. 是可不限次搭地鐵移動；與圖表原句相符，為標準答案。
passage:

subject: 英語
stem: Stacy is going to White Lake City and is staying at a hotel near the White Lake Main Station. She wants to visit the Museum of White Lake City History on Friday and see White Lake on Saturday. If she plans to buy (a) White Lake City Card(s), which of the four choices will be best for her and cost her the least?

options.C: A 1-day Card for Zone 1 and a Weekend Card for Zones 1-2.
options.D: A 1-day Card for Zones 1-2 and a Weekend Card for Zones 1-2.

explain:
解題關鍵：圖中 Main Station 和 History Museum 都在 Zone 1，週五要用平日卡，1-day Zone 1 是$20；White Lake 在 Zone 2，週六須從 Zone 1 到2，Weekend Zones 1-2 是$50。C 共$70且兩天皆涵蓋，選 C。
(A)選項原文：A 3-day Card for Zone 1. 只涵蓋 Zone 1，週六到 Zone 2 的 White Lake 不可用。
(B)選項原文：A Weekend Card for Zones 1-3. 雖能去週六行程，但 Weekend Card 只供週末與假日，不能用於週五。

(D)選項原文：A 1-day Card for Zones 1-2 and a Weekend Card for Zones 1-2. 行程可用，但週五其實只進 Zone 1，多買一級，總價$40+$50較 C 貴。

subject: 英語
stem: What is Rolling Acres?

options.C: A vacation farm.
options.D: A family restaurant.

explain:
解題關鍵：文章說 Rolling Acres 有果樹、菜園和動物，家庭可去度假、採水果、撿蛋、餵動物，正是 vacation farm（休閒農場），選 C。
(A)選項原文：A zoo. 是動物園；文中雖有動物，但還有農作物與採收活動，性質不同。
(B)選項原文：A campground. 是露營地；文章未提帳篷、露營或營地設施。
(C)選項原文：A vacation farm. 是供人休閒體驗的農場；與文中家庭度假及農場活動一致。
(D)選項原文：A family restaurant. 是家庭餐廳；沒有餐點或用餐服務的文本證據。
passage:
At 5 o’clock every morning, while most people are sleeping, 16-year-old Libby Larson is already up. She mops the floor, gets the mail and the newspapers, and gets ready for visitors to Rolling Acres. Libby’s grandparents started Rolling Acres in 1970, and since then all of the Larson family have been working there. Rolling Acres used to be just a sheep farm, but now, with its fruit trees, vegetable gardens, and many other kinds of animals, it has become a popular place for families to go on vacation. Visitors can pick fruits, collect eggs, and feed the animals. It is one of Libby’s jobs to show kids how to feed the baby sheep.

For her work, Libby is paid $10 an hour. This summer, she expects to make about $1,200 and plans to buy a cell phone. Her friends think it’s great to make that much money in a summer. However, for Libby, working at a family business also means making sacrifices. ‘I’d love to sleep until noon or go to summer camp like other kids. My friends stopped inviting me on trips because I’m always busy in the summer.’ However, Libby also said, ‘But it’s better to see both sides. Working with your family is great. You feel closer to each other.’
group_title: 人物報導：Libby 的家庭農場工作

subject: 英語
stem: What do we learn from the first paragraph?

options.A: What Libby does at Rolling Acres.
options.B: What visitors think of Rolling Acres.
options.C: Why Libby’s grandparents started Rolling Acres.
options.D: What the Larson family’s plans are for Rolling Acres.

explain:
解題關鍵：第一段先寫 Libby 清晨起床拖地、收信、準備接待訪客，又寫她教孩子餵小羊；重點是她在農場做什麼，選 A。
(A)選項原文：What Libby does at Rolling Acres. 是 Libby 在農場做的事；段落多個例子都在說明她的工作，正確。
(B)選項原文：What visitors think of Rolling Acres. 是訪客感想；文章寫他們能做哪些活動，沒有評價。
(C)選項原文：Why Libby’s grandparents started Rolling Acres. 是祖父母創辦原因；只提1970年開始，未交代原因。
(D)選項原文：What the Larson family’s plans are for Rolling Acres. 是未來計畫；段落沒有提出擴建或改變計畫。

subject: 英語
stem: What does making sacrifices mean?

options.A: Learning to make money and use it wisely.
options.B: Getting to know different sides of your family.
options.C: Making excuses for failing to do something difficult.
options.D: Giving up something important to do something else.

explain:
解題關鍵：Libby 因暑假在家族事業工作，不能睡到中午、不能去夏令營，朋友也不再邀她旅行；她為工作放棄了想做的事，making sacrifices 是選 D 的意思。
(A)選項原文：Learning to make money and use it wisely. 是學會賺錢及理財；文章有薪水，但 sacrifice 的例子不是理財。

subject: 英語
stem: What do the comics tell us?

options.B: Follow the old ways of life.
options.C: Save our planet before it’s too late.
options.D: Treat others the way we want to be treated.

explain:
解題關鍵：漫畫呈現復活節島因砍樹而乾旱、缺糧、衝突，最後一格直接說 Let’s not make Earth... another Easter Island，主旨是及時保護地球，選 C。
(A)選項原文：Enjoy life while we can. 是及時享樂；漫畫警告耗盡資源的後果，不是在鼓勵享樂。
(B)選項原文：Follow the old ways of life. 是遵循舊生活方式；故事中的舊做法正導致環境崩壞。
(C)選項原文：Save our planet before it’s too late. 是趁來得及拯救地球；與最後一格警語完全一致。
(D)選項原文：Treat others the way we want to be treated. 是待人如己；不是漫畫談論的環境主題。
passage:
1. Around the year 400, people came to Easter Island. ‘So many trees here!’
  2. They used trees to make fire and build houses. Because of the trees, people had a great life on the island.
  3. In their free time, they loved making statues with big rocks. With the trees they cut down, they could move the statues around easily.
  4. Trees were needed and used in every part of their life. Years passed, and there were fewer and fewer trees on Easter Island.
  5. Without enough trees to keep water under the ground, the land became dry, and plants didn’t grow.
  6. People began to fight for water and food. The statues were moved to fighting grounds to show their power. The last trees were probably cut down at this time.
  7. Those who cut down the last trees surely understood how important trees were to them—but still, they did it. When the last trees fell to the ground, people on the island fell, too.
  8. Let’s not make Earth, our only home, another Easter Island.
group_title: 八格漫畫：復活節島的樹木危機

subject: 英語
stem: What can we learn about the people in the comics?

options.A: They made fire before starting a fight.
options.B: They fought for land and plants all the time.
options.C: They prayed to the statues beside a large fire.
options.D: They used statues to show how strong they were.

subject: 英語
stem: What did Ariely try to find out in the origami study?

options.A: If he could stop the IKEA effect.
options.C: Why IKEA furniture is so famous.
options.D: If anyone shared his IKEA experience.

explain:
解題關鍵：第一段說 Ariely 組裝櫃子後特別喜歡它；第二段開頭明說他 wanted to know if anyone shared his feelings，因此用摺紙研究驗證是否有人有相同 IKEA experience，選 D。
(A)選項原文：If he could stop the IKEA effect. 是能否阻止此效應；研究是在觀察效應是否存在，不是要阻止它。
(B)選項原文：Why people love making origami. 是為何人們喜歡摺紙；摺紙只是實驗材料，重點是人如何估價自己的作品。
(C)選項原文：Why IKEA furniture is so famous. 是 IKEA 家具為何有名；文章沒有研究商店知名原因。
(D)選項原文：If anyone shared his IKEA experience. 是是否有人與他有相同經驗；正是第二段明示的研究目的。
passage:
Many years ago, Dan Ariely bought a cabinet from IKEA. IKEA is a famous furniture store that sells boxes of furniture parts. People who buy them have to put all the parts together themselves. It took Ariely hours to build his cabinet. Ariely didn’t really enjoy himself when he was trying to put all the parts together. However, after he finished, he felt quite good about himself and his cabinet. Later, he found that he loved his cabinet more than any of his other furniture.

Ariely wanted to know if anyone shared his feelings, so he did a fun origami study. He invited two groups of people to join his study. He called one group ‘builders’ and the other group ‘buyers.’ Builders were told to make origami, like paper frogs or paper birds. When they finished, they were asked how much they would spend on their works. Ariely then showed the origami to buyers and asked them how much they would pay for them. The two groups gave very different answers. Though buyers would pay only five cents for builders’ origami, builders would spend 25 cents! Interestingly, builders believed others would think their works were good enough to cost that much money!

Ariely’s study showed that he was not alone in his IKEA experience—we just love things more, sometimes blindly, when we make them ourselves. Ariely called it ‘the IKEA effect.’
group_title: 研究故事：IKEA effect

stem: Jerry just can’t get his daughter Mia to eat more vegetables at dinner. Every time he tries to do so, there is always a lot of shouting and crying. If Jerry wants to have Mia eat more vegetables by using the IKEA effect, what should he do?

subject: 英語
stem: What is the reading mainly about?

options.A: The tips on using a picture to tell a story.
options.B: The change that electricity brought to people’s lives.
options.C: The history behind the picture of a UK electricity worker.
options.D: The story of a famous UK electricity worker from the 1970s.

explain:
解題關鍵：文章從報紙上的英國電力工人圖片出發，說明1972、1973年兩次加薪訴求、政府措施及民眾受影響，重點是這張圖背後的歷史，選 C。
(A)選項原文：The tips on using a picture to tell a story. 是用圖片說故事的技巧；本文沒有教寫作技巧。
(B)選項原文：The change that electricity brought to people’s lives. 是電力帶來的生活改變；文章重點是罷工與限電造成的影響，不是電力發展。
(C)選項原文：The history behind the picture of a UK electricity worker. 是英國電力工人圖片背後的歷史；可涵蓋全文各段，為標準答案。
(D)選項原文：The story of a famous UK electricity worker from the 1970s. 是一位著名工人的故事；圖片代表當時工人形象，文中沒有個人傳記。
passage:
In the picture is a UK electricity worker in the 1970s. Pictures like this appeared in many newspapers at the time. In 1972, electricity workers in the UK asked to be paid more, and they decided to stop working until their wish was answered. The government worried that there wouldn’t be enough electricity for the country if these workers didn’t go to work, so it agreed to give them the pay rise. However, the story didn’t end there.

A year later, the electricity workers asked for another pay rise. To get what they wanted, they worked shorter hours and acted like they would walk away from their job anytime. But this time, the government decided to fight. To save electricity, it made new rules for people to follow. For example, each family could turn on the heat in only one room; TV stations had to stop their shows at 10:30 p.m.; businesses could open only three days a week.

People’s lives were greatly changed. Without enough heat to keep the house warm, people covered themselves in blankets all the time. Hospitals had to use candles because they couldn’t keep all the lights on. Factories couldn’t keep their machines working. Many people lost their jobs. For months, people were paying the price while the electricity workers were fighting for their wish. In the end, the government agreed to the second pay rise. This picture shows what many people thought of the electricity workers during the ‘dark’ time.

options.D: other

explain:
解題關鍵：這段回到 Cameron 國一剛開始送禮的那一年；後面又說 Now, on his birthday every year，他每年都送，因此那包餅乾是第一份 birthday gift，選 A。
(A)選項原文：first 是第一個；符合開始這個習慣時準備的第一份禮物。
(B)選項原文：last 是最後一個；他現在每年仍送禮，餅乾不可能是最後一次。
(C)選項原文：only 是唯一的；文章說他後來每年都做禮物，不是唯一一份。
(D)選項原文：other 是其他的；前面沒有另一份可供比較，且語意不通。
passage:
Most kids want gifts from their parents on their birthdays, but Cameron doesn’t. On his birthday, he gives his mom a gift. He 38 doing this in his first year of junior high school. That year, during one class, he watched a video about how a baby is pushed from its mother’s body. After class, 39. How brave a woman is to have a baby! Thank God I’ll never have to do that!

When Cameron came home that day, he held his mom in his arms for a long time. He decided that his birthday 40. During those nine months inside his mom, he just ate and slept while his mom was doing all the hard work. So why should he get a birthday gift for doing nothing? If anyone should get a gift on his birthday, it should be his mom.

The 41 ‘birthday gift’ Cameron prepared was a bag of cookies he baked. The cookies tasted so bad, but his mom said they were the best thing she ever got. Hearing that 42. It was so much better than getting a gift. Now, on his birthday every year, Cameron makes a gift for his mother to thank her for giving him life.

This year, Cameron 43 his mom a nice dress. A few months ago, he learned to make dresses at school and decided to make one for his mom. Now the dress is finished and hanging behind Cameron’s bedroom door. He believes the gift will tell his mother how much he loves her.

subject: 英語

options.C: made him change his mind
options.D: made him give up baking

explain:
解題關鍵：餅乾其實很難吃，媽媽卻說是她收過最棒的禮物；Cameron 聽到後覺得比收禮物更好，made his heart sing 指非常歡喜，選 B。
(A)選項原文：made his head hurt 是讓他頭痛；媽媽的稱讚帶來快樂，不是痛苦。
(B)選項原文：made his heart sing 是使他心裡雀躍；最能接上 It was so much better than getting a gift，為標準答案。
(C)選項原文：made him change his mind 是讓他改變主意；他後來仍每年送禮，沒有放棄原先想法。
(D)選項原文：made him give up baking 是讓他放棄烘焙；文本沒有說他不再做禮物。

subject: 英語

options.C: has given
options.D: gave

explain:
解題關鍵：洋裝已經做好，卻仍掛在 Cameron 臥室門後，表示尚未送給媽媽；他有明確計畫即將送出，要用 is going to give，選 A。
(A)選項原文：is going to give 是打算要送；有已完成的洋裝作為明顯計畫證據，正確。
(B)選項原文：gives 是現在簡單式，較像習慣或固定事實，不能凸顯這次尚未發生的送禮。
(C)選項原文：has given 是現在完成式，表示已送出；但洋裝仍藏在房門後。
(D)選項原文：gave 是過去式，也表示已經送過，和文本證據矛盾。

subject: 英語
stem: Look at the picture. All of the students who are exercising are wearing ___.

options.C: jackets
options.D: pants

explain:
解題關鍵：看圖可見所有正在運動的學生都戴著眼鏡，因此應填 glasses。題目問的是所有運動中的學生共同穿戴的物品，不是只有某一位學生有的衣物。
(A)選項原文：caps 是「帽子」；圖中不是每位運動者都戴帽子。
(B)選項原文：glasses 是「眼鏡」；每位運動中的學生都戴著，為正解。
(C)選項原文：jackets 是「外套」；圖中只有部分人物穿外套。
(D)選項原文：pants 是「長褲」；並非每位運動者都穿長褲。

subject: 英語
stem: Rita ___ her dogs many times a day. That's why they're too fat.

options.C: walks
options.D: washes

explain:
解題關鍵：狗太胖的原因最合理是 Rita 一天餵牠們太多次；主詞 Rita 是第三人稱單數，現在式動詞要用 feeds。
(A)選項原文：feeds 是「餵食」，能直接解釋狗變胖，為正解。
(B)選項原文：kisses 是「親吻」；親吻不會使狗變胖。
(C)選項原文：walks 是「帶著散步」；多散步反而不符合太胖的原因。
(D)選項原文：washes 是「清洗」；洗澡與體重無直接關係。

subject: 英語
stem: You can ask Sophia anything about butterflies and bees. She has great ___ of insects.

options.C: news
options.D: power

explain:
解題關鍵：任何蝴蝶、蜜蜂的問題都能問 Sophia，表示她具備豐富的昆蟲知識。固定說法是 have knowledge of...。
(A)選項原文：chances 是「機會」，不能說有很多昆蟲的機會。
(B)選項原文：knowledge 是「知識」；have great knowledge of insects 表示很懂昆蟲，為正解。
(C)選項原文：news 是「消息」，不是對一門主題的理解能力。
(D)選項原文：power 是「力量、權力」，與回答昆蟲問題無關。

subject: 英語
stem: Adam slept ___ last night because he kept waking up from bad dreams.

options.C: terribly
options.D: quickly

explain:
解題關鍵：Adam 一直被惡夢驚醒，睡眠品質很差；空格修飾動詞 slept，要用副詞 terribly，意為「很糟地」。
(A)選項原文：deeply 是「深沉地」；與不斷醒來相反。
(B)選項原文：early 是「早地」；只說時間早，不說睡得好不好。
(C)選項原文：terribly 是「糟糕地」；最能呼應 bad dreams，為正解。
(D)選項原文：quickly 是「快速地」；不能自然描述睡眠品質。

subject: 英語
stem: Tara enjoys being with all kinds of animals; she even ___ a snake as a pet.

options.C: keeps
options.D: makes

explain:
解題關鍵：把蛇當寵物，要表達「飼養」；主詞 she 為第三人稱單數，所以用 keeps。
(A)選項原文：drops 是「掉下、放下」，不能表示養寵物。
(B)選項原文：gives 是「給予」，後面直接接 a snake as a pet 語意不通。
(C)選項原文：keeps 是「飼養、留著」；keep a snake as a pet 正確，為正解。
(D)選項原文：makes 是「製作、使成為」；蛇不是她製作出來的。

subject: 英語
stem: Little Eric chose the doll ___ big brown eyes because it was the cutest in the store.

options.C: on
options.D: with

explain:
解題關鍵：要修飾 doll 的外觀特徵，英文用 with + 名詞，the doll with big brown eyes 表示「有大棕色眼睛的娃娃」。
(A)選項原文：at 通常表地點或目標，如 look at，不可用來連接外觀特徵。
(B)選項原文：in 表示「在……裡」，不合 doll 與 eyes 的關係。
(C)選項原文：on 表示「在……上面」；不能說 doll on big brown eyes。
(D)選項原文：with 表示「有、帶著」；用來描述娃娃具有眼睛，為正解。

subject: 英語
stem: After four hours of mountain climbing, Rosa's legs got ___, so she took a rest on the top of the mountain.

options.C: sore
options.D: strong

explain:
解題關鍵：爬山四小時後需要在山頂休息，原因是腿部痠痛；get sore 可表示「變得痠痛」。
(A)選項原文：dirty 是「髒的」；腿髒不一定需要因而休息。
(B)選項原文：sick 是「生病、不舒服的」；通常形容人，不是運動後的腿部痠痛。
(C)選項原文：sore 是「痠痛的」；最符合長時間爬山後腿的狀態，為正解。
(D)選項原文：strong 是「強壯的」；腿變強壯反而不合 took a rest 的原因。

subject: 英語
stem: Having three cups of coffee a day can't be bad for our health, ___?

options.C: is it
options.D: are they

explain:
解題關鍵：附加問句要重複前面子句的助動詞 can。Having three cups of coffee a day 是一整個動名詞片語，視為單數，所以代名詞用 it；原句有否定 can't，附加問句改肯定 can it。
(A)選項原文：can it 同時保留 can 並以 it 代替動名詞片語，為正解。
(B)選項原文：can they 的 they 是複數，不能代替單數動名詞片語。
(C)選項原文：is it 用的是 be 動詞；原句的助動詞是 can。
(D)選項原文：are they 同時用了錯誤助動詞與複數代名詞。

subject: 英語
stem: You can't push that door open with only one hand. It's too heavy. You have to use ___!

options.C: both
options.D: one

explain:
解題關鍵：前句說 only one hand 推不開門，後句自然是要用「兩隻手」，因此填 both。
(A)選項原文：all 是「全部」，通常指三個以上或全體，不是剛好兩手。
(B)選項原文：another 是「另一個」，只能補上一隻手，仍不等於兩隻都用。
(C)選項原文：both 是「兩者都」；use both 指兩隻手一起用，為正解。
(D)選項原文：one 是「一個」；正與題幹說的一隻手不夠相衝突。

subject: 英語
stem: Alan works hard in his new job, and he wants to know ___ his boss feels about him.

options.C: whether
options.D: why

explain:
解題關鍵：Alan 想知道老闆「對他感覺如何」，常用 how + 人 + feels about...；how 引導 know 後面的名詞子句。
(A)選項原文：how 表示「如何」；how his boss feels about him 正確，為正解。
(B)選項原文：that 只連接陳述內容，that his boss feels about him 缺少感覺的方式。
(C)選項原文：whether 表示「是否」；後面應有完整的 yes/no 內容，不能直接接 feels about him。
(D)選項原文：why 是「為什麼」；題意問的是老闆的看法，不是感受的原因。

subject: 英語
stem: I thought the girl ___ was Kate, but it was her sister, Candy. They sounded almost the same.

options.C: who answered the phone
options.D: and answered the phone

explain:
解題關鍵：空格要補充說明是哪一位女孩接電話；先行詞 the girl 是人，且 who 在子句中當 answered 的主詞，所以用 who answered the phone。
(A)選項原文：answered the phone 缺少子句主詞，不能直接修飾 the girl。
(B)選項原文：she answered the phone 有自己的主詞 she；放在 the girl 後會形成兩個主詞，缺少連接詞。
(C)選項原文：who answered the phone 是關係子句，who 指 the girl，為正解。
(D)選項原文：and answered the phone 是並列連接，會把 I thought the girl 和 answered 錯誤並列，句構不通。

subject: 英語
stem: Ken is going abroad with a woman he met online, though he doesn't know ___ well.

options.C: any
options.D: another

explain:
解題關鍵：空格放在 know 後面，須當受詞，指前面的 a woman，因此用受格代名詞 her。
(A)選項原文：her 是「她」的受格，可作 know 的受詞，為正解。
(B)選項原文：each other 是「彼此」；需有兩方互相做動作，Ken 單方面不認識她不適用。
(C)選項原文：any 不能單獨指這一位已提到的女子。
(D)選項原文：another 是「另一個」，會變成不知道另一位女子，與題幹不符。

subject: 英語
stem: Joe is happy he is not at the ___ of the class now. His grades are better than half of his classmates' this school year.

options.C: center
options.D: bottom

explain:
解題關鍵：Joe 的成績比一半同學好，表示已不在班上最低的位置。固定說法 at the bottom of the class 是「班上墊底」。
(A)選項原文：side 是「旁邊」；at the side of the class 不表示成績排名。
(B)選項原文：front 是「前面」；若在前段，會與 only better than half 的資訊不精確。
(C)選項原文：center 是「中央」；不表示成績末段。
(D)選項原文：bottom 是「底部、末位」；not at the bottom 表示不再墊底，為正解。

subject: 英語
stem: Look! There is not a cloud in the sky. I think the chances of getting some rain today are really ___.

options.C: possible
options.D: small

explain:
解題關鍵：天空完全沒有雲，今天下雨的機率應很低；chances are small 是「機率很小」的自然搭配。
(A)選項原文：far 是「遠的」；不能形容 chances 的大小。
(B)選項原文：good 是「好的」；good chances 表示機會很高，與無雲線索相反。
(C)選項原文：possible 是「可能的」；文法上可說 possible，但不表達機率很低，且 really possible 不合語意。
(D)選項原文：small 是「小的」；small chances 表示下雨機率小，為正解。

subject: 英語
stem: On windy days, the flowers in my garden ___ like shy children with their heads down.

options.C: rise
options.D: smell

explain:
解題關鍵：風天裡花朵像害羞孩子般低著頭，bow 可作動詞表示「低頭鞠躬」，最能描寫這個姿勢。
(A)選項原文：bow 是「低頭、鞠躬」；與 heads down 的畫面吻合，為正解。
(B)選項原文：fall 是「掉落」；花會垂低但題幹不是說掉下來。
(C)選項原文：rise 是「升起」；與低頭方向相反。
(D)選項原文：smell 是「聞起來有……氣味」；不能接 like shy children 描寫動作。

subject: 英語
stem: Mr. Olson went to the doctor when he found he ___ his hair. He hoped he would be able to keep his thick hair.

options.C: will lose
options.D: has lost

explain:
解題關鍵：Mr. Olson 去看醫生並發現自己掉髮，兩事都在過去；掉髮是他當時正在經歷的持續狀況，所以用過去進行式 was losing。
(A)選項原文：was losing 是過去某時正在掉髮，與 went、found 的時間一致，為正解。
(B)選項原文：is losing 是現在進行式，和過去式 found 時間不一致。
(C)選項原文：will lose 是未來式，題幹已說他發現正在發生的問題。
(D)選項原文：has lost 是現在完成式；雖可說已掉了一些頭髮，但不如過去進行式精確表達發現當下的過程。

subject: 英語
stem: Do you know what Lindsey's first job was? Before becoming a movie star, she ___ the floors at the supermarket.

options.C: has mopped
options.D: mopped

explain:
解題關鍵：Lindsey 成為電影明星之前的第一份工作是已結束的過去經歷，因此用過去式 mopped。
(A)選項原文：mops 是現在式，像在說她現在仍每天拖地。
(B)選項原文：is mopping 是現在進行式，與 before becoming a movie star 的過去背景不合。
(C)選項原文：has mopped 是現在完成式，強調從過去延續到現在，不合已成為明星前的工作。
(D)選項原文：mopped 是過去式，表示她當時在超市拖地，為正解。

subject: 英語
stem: Our dog Lassie hides under the bed every time the moon comes out. She has been ___ for years, but we don't know why.

options.C: like us
options.D: that

explain:
解題關鍵：狗每逢月亮出來就躲床底，後句是在說牠多年來一直「像這樣」行為；has been like this 是描述持續狀態的正確搭配。
(A)選項原文：it 不能單獨放在 has been 後指代這種行為。
(B)選項原文：like this 是「像這樣」；指前述躲床底的習慣，為正解。
(C)選項原文：like us 是「像我們」；人與狗的比較不合上下文。
(D)選項原文：that 單獨置於 has been 後不自然，也未清楚指行為方式。

subject: 英語
stem:
Tom: Sam, could you help me in the kitchen now?
Sam: No, I ___ TV. It's the most important game of the season.

options.C: have watched
options.D: am watching

explain:
解題關鍵：Tom 問 now 能不能幫忙，Sam 說正在看本季最重要的比賽，表示動作正在說話當下進行，要用現在進行式 am watching。
(A)選項原文：watch 是現在簡單式，較像固定習慣，沒有強調此刻。
(B)選項原文：watched 是過去式，不能解釋現在無法幫忙。
(C)選項原文：have watched 是現在完成式，表示已看過，不表示正在看。
(D)選項原文：am watching 是現在進行式，呼應 now，為正解。

subject: 英語
stem: Amanda wants to make fruit tea by following The Best Fruit Tea You Can Make at Home. She has several kinds of fruit in the kitchen: apples, bananas, oranges, papayas, pears, and strawberries. Which are some of the fruits she can use to make the fruit tea?

options.C: Apples, oranges and strawberries.
options.D: Bananas, papayas and strawberries.

explain:
解題關鍵：食譜的 Note 明說 Most fruits are good, but not papayas or bananas。檢查每組水果，只有 C 同時避開 papayas 與 bananas，故可使用。
(A)選項原文：Oranges, papayas and pears. 含有 papayas，文章明定不可用。
(B)選項原文：Apples, bananas and oranges. 含有 bananas，文章明定不可用。
(C)選項原文：Apples, oranges and strawberries. 三種都不是 papayas 或 bananas，為正解。
(D)選項原文：Bananas, papayas and strawberries. 同時含 bananas 與 papayas，違反食譜提醒。
passage:
The Best Fruit Tea You Can Make at Home
http://www.fruitteaDIY.com

Things to get ready:
3-4 teabags (green or black tea), half an apple, half a peach, half a pear, 20 mL lemon juice, 1,200 mL water, 30 g sugar

Note: Most fruits are good for making fruit tea, but not papayas or bananas.

How to make fruit tea:

  1. Boil a pot of water.
  2. Put the teabags into the pot of hot water for 2 to 3 minutes and take them out.
  3. Cut the fruit into small pieces.
  4. Put the pieces into the hot tea and wait for another 5 to 6 minutes. (Leave the fruit in the pot to make the tea taste better.)
  5. Put in sugar and lemon juice and stir for at least 10 seconds.

Now enjoy the tea!

The Best Fruit Tea You Can Make at Home
http://www.fruitteaDIY.com

Things to get ready:
3-4 teabags (green or black tea), half an apple, half a peach, half a pear, 20 mL lemon juice, 1,200 mL water, 30 g sugar

explain:
解題關鍵：Harrison 拉大提琴時夜鶯會一起唱，之後她在廣播中與這些夜鶯演出長達十二年；她因「和夜鶯一起演奏」聞名，才被稱為 Nightingale Lady。

(B)選項原文：She sang as beautifully as a nightingale did. Harrison 演奏的是 cello，不是唱歌。
(C)選項原文：She taught nightingales to sing in a radio show. 夜鶯自行飛來唱，並非她教牠們。

passage:
One summer evening when English cello player Beatrice Harrison was practicing in her garden, she was joined by a visitor she did not expect.

The visitor was a nightingale. The small brown bird sang together with Harrison's cello music, and the birdsong sounded like the piece she was playing. For the next few evenings, her visitor kept coming back, sometimes with several of its friends. Harrison decided that more people should hear the little singers.

So, on May 19, 1924, Harrison worked with the BBC, the UK's national TV and radio station, and played in her garden. At first, the artist was playing alone. Fifteen minutes before the end of her playing, the nightingales began to sing with the cello.

The nightingale show was popular with radio listeners. It was repeated the next week, and for the next twelve years Harrison played on the radio with her garden friends. During this time, she got 50,000 fan letters. People called her "the Nightingale Lady."

passage:
With heavy hearts, we are here to say goodbye to Rose Lacey, a wonderful writer who will be sadly missed.

Rose and I first met in 2010. I was at a party to pick up my wife when I heard Rose explaining to her and her friends why Get Across was a great movie. Her ideas were so interesting that I invited her to write some articles about movies for Action! US. Rose was very excited and agreed right away.

Over the next ten years, Rose wrote more than 150 articles. Rose could always bring out something new from movies that we thought we knew so well. People often told me that Rose never failed to surprise them. Her articles often made them think whether they actually saw the same movie, but if they went to see it again, they experienced the movie in a whole new way.

In her short life of 40 years, Rose has made her mark on the world of movies with her articles for Action! US. We are lucky to have had her in our lives. She was a very special person.

Alex Jackson
Head of Action! US

subject: 英語
stem: Why does the title say "Glass Bottles' Second Life"?

options.A: People collect sea glass and use it to make new glass bottles.
options.B: People collect sea glass at the beach and use it to make wishes.
options.C: Glass bottles that are thrown into the sea become the homes of sea animals.
options.D: Glass bottles that are thrown into the sea become sea glass which is used in art pieces.

explain:
解題關鍵：圖文說明玻璃瓶被丟進海裡後撞碎、磨圓、外層變白成 sea glass，最後又被藝術家放入作品；原本是垃圾的瓶子以海玻璃形式再被使用，所以叫 Second Life。
(A)選項原文：People collect sea glass and use it to make new glass bottles. 文章說用於 art pieces，沒有做成新瓶子。
(B)選項原文：People collect sea glass at the beach and use it to make wishes. 沒有許願的資訊。
(C)選項原文：Glass bottles that are thrown into the sea become the homes of sea animals. 文中沒有海洋動物住進瓶子的過程。
(D)選項原文：Glass bottles that are thrown into the sea become sea glass which is used in art pieces. 完整對應流程與用途，為正解。
passage:
SEA GLASS: GLASS BOTTLES' SECOND LIFE

Sea glass is made from the magic of the sea. It usually comes from glass bottles that are thrown into the water. Each piece of sea glass looks different, and sea glass is often seen on art pieces. The pictures below explain how sea glass is born.

  1. Glass bottles are thrown as garbage into the sea.
  2. When these bottles ride the waves of the sea, they hit each other or other garbage in the sea and break into small pieces of glass.
  3. Pieces of glass are pushed by sea water and move along the sea floor. The sharp pieces slowly become rounder and rounder.
  4. After tens or hundreds of years in the sea, the pieces of glass grow an ice-like white color on the outside and become sea glass.
  5. Sea glass is finally pushed up to the beach.
  6. Artists collect pieces of sea glass and put them into their works.

However, people now seldom use glass to make bottles and bowls—paper bowls and cups have become more popular these days. This means there are fewer glass items in the sea, so less and less sea glass will be found in the future.

passage:
SEA GLASS: GLASS BOTTLES' SECOND LIFE

Sea glass is made from the magic of the sea. It usually comes from glass bottles that are thrown into the water. Each piece of sea glass looks different, and sea glass is often seen on art pieces. The pictures below explain how sea glass is born.

  1. Glass bottles are thrown as garbage into the sea.
  2. When these bottles ride the waves of the sea, they hit each other or other garbage in the sea and break into small pieces of glass.
  3. Pieces of glass are pushed by sea water and move along the sea floor. The sharp pieces slowly become rounder and rounder.
  4. After tens or hundreds of years in the sea, the pieces of glass grow an ice-like white color on the outside and become sea glass.
  5. Sea glass is finally pushed up to the beach.
  6. Artists collect pieces of sea glass and put them into their works.

However, people now seldom use glass to make bottles and bowls—paper bowls and cups have become more popular these days. This means there are fewer glass items in the sea, so less and less sea glass will be found in the future.

passage:
The Future of Icelandic　Scandinavian News　by Anna Adams

Icelandic is a language that is spoken only in Iceland. It has a long history. But many Icelanders are worried that they're losing Icelandic.

The reason for their worry is the prevalence of English in Iceland. "I use English when I talk to my housework robot, use my phone, and watch movies," said Helgi Atlason, an engineer. There is a reason for that. Most of these products use English, and few companies care to change the language into Icelandic because there are only a small number of Icelandic speakers (314,000 people). Actually, you see English everywhere in Iceland.

Icelanders also speak and hear more English than Icelandic these days because many foreigners who come to live and work in Iceland speak only English. "We can't use Icelandic abroad, and we're not using it much in Iceland, either. How do you expect our kids will want to learn it?" said Eirikur Wilson, a teacher.

Will Iceland one day give up Icelandic for English? It may happen soon.

Our Future with Icelandic　Scandinavian News　by Gunnar Eggertsson

Many people think Icelandic is a language in its sickbed and that it needs to be saved. I understand their worries, but does the future of our language really look that bad?

According to Dr. David Clingingsmith, a language needs at least 35,000 speakers to be "safe" from becoming a dying language. There are now 314,000 Icelandic speakers. Also, every year Iceland spends 51.3 million Icelandic crowns (3.7 million US dollars) teaching Icelandic to machines: phones, computers, and robots. Icelandic is appearing more often in products. Most importantly, schools still teach Icelandic to children. Clearly, we are not giving up our first language.

However, I'm not saying that Iceland has done enough for Icelandic. Our country can do a better job at getting more people to speak this beautiful language. One way to do so is to give more language courses to foreigners. With much more work, I'm sure Icelandic can grow and even reach farther into the world.

passage:
A long time ago, there was an old king who had no child of his own. The king was worried that his land would fall into the wrong hands after his death, so he decided to pick a child in his land to take the high seat. One day, he called all the children to his castle and gave each of them a seed. "Come back on New Year's Day and show me what you have grown," he said to them, "and I will 40 ."

Every child brought their seeds home carefully. One of the children, Wong, planted his seed in a pot. He gave it water every day and made sure there was sun to help it grow. 41 .

Then, Sung, the child of the richest family in the land, told people that a small plant was growing from his seed. He was 42 . Everyone excitedly said that he would be king. Soon, one after another, more and more children were also saying that they had something in their pots. But Wong still didn't find anything in his.

On the big day, when Wong brought his pot to the castle, he saw all the other children carrying interesting plants. Some had flowers in the shape of a bird, and some had grasses of different colors. Everyone proudly showed their plants to the king, but the king looked unhappy until he saw Wong's pot. "I boiled the seeds before I gave them out, so no plants could grow from them." The king looked seriously at the children. "There is only one child who is 43 enough to be king."

Ten years later, the king died. On his deathbed, he was not worried because he knew Wong would be a good king.

The king looked seriously at the children. "There is only one child who is 43 enough to be king."

Ten years later, the king died. On his deathbed, he was not worried because he knew Wong would be a good king.

**1**. 「趁老農夫不在，彼得小兔溜進了菜園裡大快朵頤。他先吃點青翠新鮮的萵苣，再吃些碧綠滾圓的青豆子，最後啃著鮮嫩多汁的紅蘿蔔。風裡透著泥土的甜香，小鳥兒唱著醉人的音符，遍地的蔬菜又大又肥——彼得小兔________。」根據這段文字的語境，畫線處填入下列何者最恰當？

- (A) 一臉困惑的抓著頭皮，不知所措
- (B) 興奮的窮追不捨，不讓獵物脫逃
- (C) 臨風顧盼，心滿意足的摸著肚子 🟢 (正解)
- (D) 拱起背脊，屏氣
